Verified: deno check+lint clean, 2 tests pass. STILL passes:false: AC2 (the explicit Stripe lead-time is a Dashboard billing setting — Settings->Billing->Upcoming renewal reminders — not code) and AC5's live half (an annual sub actually producing a reminder before renewal needs a Stripe run). AC1/AC3/AC4 are done (handleInvoiceUpcoming + handleTrialWillEnd wired, transactional category, now guarded).

userStories.title: iOS paywall advertises 1,000 AI actions for Pro; the server grants 750
userStories.description: ios/GradeThread/Billing/IAPProduct.swift:88,93 advertises Pro as '1,000 listings · 1,000 AI actions · 30 grades · AutoLister'. Both the server catalog (services/edge-functions/src/lib/appstore/products.ts:75,80) and web (src/lib/constants.ts:243, aiActionsPerMonth: 750) say 750. iOS buyers are sold 1,000 AI actions and will be plan-gated at 750 — a paid-for entitlement that does not exist. The drift test that should catch this (iap-catalog-drift_test.ts:69-106) compares ids, credits, plan/interval and fallbackPrice but NOT blurb or title, so the guard has a hole exactly where the misleading copy lives.
acceptanceCriteria: Correct the iOS copy to match the entitlement actually granted (or change the entitlement — but the two must agree).
Extend iap-catalog-drift_test.ts to compare user-facing blurb and title against the server catalog, so advertised entitlements cannot drift from granted ones.
Audit every other advertised number on the paywall against the server catalog.
Check whether any user purchased Pro on iOS under the 1,000 copy and determine remediation with the review gate.

userStories.title: No price-change notice or consent path on any platform
userStories.description: No code path notifies a user of a price increase before it takes effect. Stripe's price.updated and customer.subscription.updated-with-price-delta are not inspected (webhooks.ts:244-281). On Apple, the ASSN router (lib/appstore/notifications.ts:18-32) does not handle PRICE_INCREASE or DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF — Apple collects price-increase consent natively so this is not a rejection risk, but the server never learns a price change occurred, and an unconsented lapse arrives only as a generic EXPIRED. On Google Play, PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is explicitly a no-op (lib/google-play/rtdn.ts:11,107).
acceptanceCriteria: Notify subscribers in advance of any price increase, stating the old price, new price, effective date and how to cancel first.
Handle Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF so server state reflects platform-side changes.
Decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web (it commonly does under state ARLs) and implement accordingly.
Do not implement a price change of any kind until this exists.

The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Currently latent — no price change has been attempted. It becomes a live exposure the moment pricing moves, which makes it cheap to fix now and expensive to fix under deadline. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (mechanism — no counsel). Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF now reach server state. routeNotification gained a THIRD kind of verdict, record_only, distinct from both an entitlement action and 'ignore'. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Apple owns price-increase consent natively, so ACTING on these would be wrong — if the customer refuses, Apple lapses the subscription and we hear EXPIRED. But ignoring them meant that later EXPIRED was uninterpretable: indistinguishable from an ordinary cancellation, with no way to tell that a price change preceded it. Recording without acting is exactly the right posture, and it is the same 'known-ignored vs unexamined' distinction I built for the Stripe switch in US-2128 — the two surfaces had the identical defect. REUSED recordAppstoreEvent rather than hand-rolling the insert: it already namespaces stripe_event_id as appstore:<id> and swallows 23505, so an Apple retry cannot double-record. (My first attempt DID hand-roll it — the helper was 180 lines above and I had not looked. Worth noting because writing the second copy is always easier than finding the first.) 4 tests, including the two that matter: record_only must NOT be an entitlement action (not sub_active, not sub_expired, not revoke), and an unknown type must STILL fail closed to ignore — widening a router is exactly when a permissive default sneaks in. REMAINING, and correctly split: AC1 (notify subscribers in advance of an increase) needs the COPY, which is US-2114's gate — but note the DETECTION half is now free: US-2117's migration 00486 added pricing_plan_revisions, an append-only price history written BY TRIGGER, so 'a price changed' is already a queryable fact rather than something needing new plumbing. AC3 is explicitly a decision ('decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web') and belongs to counsel. AC4 is a CONSTRAINT rather than work — do not ship a price change until AC1/AC3 exist — and is worth keeping visible: the pricing_plans trigger will now record any change, so an accidental one leaves evidence. Google Play PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is still a no-op (rtdn.ts) and is the same shape as the Apple fix if someone wants symmetry. Verified: edge 4310 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC2 EXTENDED TO GOOGLE PLAY — the symmetry I flagged last pass, and it turned out to be the SHARPER of the two platforms. Apple's PRICE_INCREASE is a notification that a price WILL change; Google's PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is the user ACCEPTING one. That makes it a consent artifact — exactly what subscription_agreements (US-2117) exists to hold — and dropping it meant the only server-side evidence of the acceptance was the eventual renewal amount, which is an INFERENCE rather than a record. classifyRtdn now returns record_only for type 8, and the reconciler writes an audit row via the existing recordEvent dep (idempotent on the event id) while touching no entitlement: Google owns the consent UI, so acting would pre-empt it, and the next renewal RTDN settles the amount. ADDED A DISTINCT OUTCOME VALUE rather than reusing 'ignored': both leave entitlement untouched, but one wrote an audit row and the other did not. Collapsing them would leave the RTDN log unable to answer 'did we ever learn the user accepted a price change?' — which is the entire point of the branch. TWO THINGS THE TYPE SYSTEM AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT, both of them the system working: (1) adding the union variant broke the route glue's narrowing at `action.productType`, which is TypeScript correctly refusing to let a new action fall through unhandled; (2) an existing test asserted type 8 → ignore and went RED, correctly — it was encoding the old behaviour, and it was right to fail rather than let the change pass silently. Updated it to state WHY 8 left that group, so the next reader sees the reasoning rather than an unexplained gap in [9,10,11]. PROCESS NOTE: this took four attempts because bash ate template literals and regex escapes in inline node -e scripts (the fifth such incident today). Anything containing backticks or regex now goes through the Edit tool, not a shell string. Verified: edge 4312 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Unhandled Stripe subscription webhooks including payment_action_required
userStories.description: The webhook switch (webhooks.ts:244-281) covers the core lifecycle well — subscription created/updated/paused/resumed/deleted, invoice.payment_succeeded/failed, checkout.session.completed, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created/closed — with solid infrastructure (idempotency claims, fail-closed metrics, transient-vs-permanent error split). Everything else hits a default log-and-drop. Unhandled and consequential: invoice.upcoming and customer.subscription.trial_will_end (covered by their own stories), invoice.payment_action_required (SCA/3DS — the user is never told a payment needs authorization and simply fails), invoice.finalized, checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded/_failed (already flagged in a code comment as a live risk if non-card payment methods are enabled), price.updated, payment_method.attached/detached.
acceptanceCriteria: Handle invoice.payment_action_required and notify the user that action is needed, with a link to complete authentication.
Handle the async payment-method events before enabling any non-card payment method.
Review the remaining unhandled events and either handle or explicitly document each as intentionally ignored, so the default branch means 'known-ignored' rather than 'unexamined'.
userStories.notes: [P2][Billing/Reliability] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. Not a disclosure issue — filed alongside because it is the same webhook surface and a silent SCA failure looks to the user like an unexplained loss of service. Dunning otherwise is genuinely thorough (US-395 grace clock, Smart Retries, fail-closed to Free). | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC3 DONE; AC2 correctly deferred. AC1: invoice.payment_action_required is now handled and the user is told. That event was the WORST one to be silent about, and the reason is specific — an ordinary failed payment is driven by Stripe's Smart Retries, so it self-heals or escalates on its own, whereas an SCA/3DS challenge waits on a HUMAN who has been told nothing. Same end state to the user (service degrades), completely different remedy (complete a bank challenge, not update a card). New sendPaymentActionRequiredEmail is DELIBERATELY a separate template rather than reusing the payment-failed one: sending 'update your card' here points someone at the wrong fix and leaves the real one undone. It links Stripe's hosted_invoice_url, which is where the challenge is actually completed — an email telling someone their payment needs action with no way to take it would be worse than silence. DELIBERATELY DOES NOT flip subscription_status to past_due: Stripe fires invoice.payment_failed if the authentication is never completed, and THAT event owns the dunning clock. Starting the grace period from two events would make past_due_since depend on delivery ORDER. Mirrors the payment-failed handler's shape throughout (same customer resolution, same US-1799 buyer skip, same event ledger, same safeSendEmail) rather than inventing a parallel one. AC3: the default branch now distinguishes KNOWN-IGNORED from UNEXAMINED. Previously one log line covered both facts, which meant a newly-enabled Stripe feature could start firing a consequential event and read exactly like the routine noise beside it. INTENTIONALLY_IGNORED_EVENTS lists 16 events with the reason each is dropped; anything NOT on it now warns AND records a webhook.unexpected_event metric. Note the two story-owned events (invoice.upcoming, customer.subscription.trial_will_end) are LISTED rather than merely absent — being ignored HERE because another surface owns them is a decision worth recording, not a gap. 5 tests, including the one that catches the likely future mistake: a handled event must never ALSO appear on the ignored list, since that combination would mean someone added a handler without removing the entry and the list would be lying about what happens. AC2 (async payment-method events) NOT done and should not be: those matter only once a non-card payment method is enabled, and pre-writing handlers for a payment method nobody has turned on is speculative work of exactly the kind that produced this codebase's dead modules. The AC itself says 'before enabling any non-card payment method' — that is the trigger, and it has not fired. Verified: edge 4283 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-22 FOLLOW-UP FIX (agent loop): a completeness guard caught that payment_action_required — the SCA/3DS notice AC1 added — was NEVER registered in TRANSACTIONAL_CATEGORIES (email-transport.ts), even though the note says the handler "mirrors the payment-failed handler's shape throughout" and payment_failed IS in the set. Effect was LATENT not live (sendPaymentActionRequiredEmail passes no marketing flag, so resolveIsMarketing defaulted it transactional), but it lacked the force-classification GUARANTEE the AC6 protection gives every other required billing notice — i.e. if it were ever routed with marketing:true or the identity/unsubscribe logic keyed off membership, the one notice that owns an SCA challenge could be marketing-classified. Added payment_action_required to the set (defense-in-depth + consistency), and added a COMPLETENESS guard in email-transport_test.ts asserting all four required billing notices (trial_expiring, subscription_renewal_reminder, payment_action_required, payment_failed) are members — the prior AC6 test only checked members OF the set, so removing a required one from it passed silently. That guard is what surfaced this. Verified: deno check+lint clean, 13 email-transport tests pass. (US-2128 stays passes:false: AC2 async-payment-method events remain a documented tripwire for when a non-card method is enabled.)

userStories.title: Authenticity prompt activation must fail closed — the eval gate has never run
userStories.description: services/edge-functions/src/lib/ai-authenticity.ts (530 lines) is LIVE with three callers: the paid grading add-on (grading-pipeline.ts:1239), the buyer credit-metered check (routes/buyer-authenticity.ts:53), and an UNAUTHENTICATED public endpoint (routes/public-grading.ts:998). Results surface on public certificates. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts (268 lines) — the accuracy gate — has zero non-self callers. Its own header states: '⚠ THIS GATE DOES NOT RUN... Do not read this module's green tests as evidence the gate exists.' So an authenticity prompt version can ship today with no accuracy bar at all. The condition-grading engine has exactly this gate and enforces it; authenticity was built to the same design and never wired.
acceptanceCriteria: Wire runAuthenticityEval into the authenticity prompt-activation path, mirroring how the grading engine gates prompt versions (shadow -> eval gate -> canary).
Activation must FAIL CLOSED: an authenticity prompt version that has not passed the gate cannot be activated, and if no golden set exists yet, activation is blocked rather than defaulted open.
Add the admin route/surface needed to run the eval and view results.
Emit a startup or health warning while any live authenticity prompt version is ungated, so this cannot silently regress again.
Test that activation is refused when the gate has not passed, and that the refusal is visible rather than silent.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Safety][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. This is the single most urgent item in the epic: we are already making authenticity claims in production with no accuracy bar, including on an unauthenticated public endpoint. Same risk class as the FTC Section 5 substantiation work (US-2114..2128). Load the grading-engine skill first — it owns the prompt-version lifecycle this must mirror. Related: US-1996 tracks the backlog-integrity side of the same gap. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: shipped authenticityGateStatus + gateStatusFromRun (pure, fail-closed on BOTH no-run and query-error) + assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable (the fail-closed guard a future activation path must call) + warnAuthenticityGate wired into main.ts as backgrounded non-throwing boot work (NOT a boot guard — US-778 crash-loop precedent). Model is part of the gate key, mirroring US-2036. Guard test extended: accepts either runAuthenticityEval or assertAuthenticityPromptActivatable, and now pins the boot check. 4348 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: (a) no authenticity prompt-ACTIVATION path exists to block — authenticity prompts are code constants, not ai_prompt_versions rows; building that lifecycle needs a migration and was deliberately NOT invented here (see the reasoning in authenticity-gate-guard_test.ts, which argues against speculative lifecycles); (b) the gate will report ungated for every version until US-2131 seeds real labeled cases. Next: admin route to RUN the eval. ITER2 2026-07-19: added GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/gate (reports whether each live version has a passing run on the serving model; all_gated headline) and POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/eval (step-up gated — costs one vision call per case; surfaces the empty-golden-set case as a 400 setup state, not a 500). Reused the existing admin group so guards/audit are inherited. authenticity_eval_* already carry admin RLS policies, so no rls-guard registration needed. 4348 edge tests pass.

userStories.title: Build the authenticity golden set — the gate is worthless without ground truth
userStories.description: authenticity_eval_cases (00405_authenticity_eval.sql) exists but has NO seed rows anywhere in the repo — by design, the golden set is operator-curated. runAuthenticityEval would throw on first call (authenticity-eval.ts:183). This is the expensive, slow, expert-dependent asset that everything else in the epic depends on, and it cannot be generated by an agent: it requires labeled authentic-vs-counterfeit items with real photos and defensible provenance for each label.
acceptanceCriteria: Define what a case requires: photos at the resolution the pipeline actually receives, the ground-truth label, the provenance of that label (who determined it and how), brand, garment type, and the tells that justify the label.
Build the operator curation surface for adding, reviewing and retiring cases.
Set the passing bar with counsel/product input — including the false-positive bar, which matters far more than overall accuracy: calling a genuine item fake is the more damaging error.
Seed an initial set covering the brands we actually see most, not the brands that are most interesting.
Track per-brand coverage so the gate cannot pass on a brand it has never seen.
Follow the grading-engine skill's golden-set rules and exemplar-privacy constraints.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Data][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. USER/EXPERT ACTION REQUIRED — an agent can build the surface and the schema, but not the labels. This is the true critical path for the whole epic; sequence accordingly. Sourcing options to evaluate: partner with an authentication service, buy a labeled corpus, or curate from our own human-review history where provenance is defensible. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: the CURATION SURFACE is built — GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases, needing NO migration because 00405 already carries every column including source_url for label provenance. Deliberately NO delete route: per the grading-engine contract a shrinking golden set is a red flag, and deleting the cases a prompt fails is the easiest way to fake a pass — cases are RETIRED (is_active=false) and every ground-truth change is audited. validateAuthenticityCase rejects empty images at write time rather than letting runAuthenticityEval throw mid-run after spending vision calls on earlier cases. summarizeCaseCoverage marks a brand usable ONLY with at least one authentic AND one counterfeit case: a perfect score over authentic-only cases cannot demonstrate the one error the gate exists to catch. 4357 edge tests pass. STILL BLOCKED: the labels themselves. An expert must now add real cases through this surface; nothing downstream (the gate passing, US-2134 prompt narrowing, US-2143 positioning) can move until they exist. ITER 2026-07-19: bulk import shipped — lib/golden-set-import.ts + POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/cases/import, plus docs/authenticity-golden-set-template.json. Partial success is REPORTED per row (index + reason) and does not fail the batch: re-uploading 50 rows over one typo is how people start bypassing validation. Returns 207 when any row was rejected, 201 when clean, and a rejected count is always present so a caller can tell a partial from a full success without parsing counts. brand_key is alias-resolved via brandKeyForRaw, so an import written "Levi Strauss" lands on the same key as the KB row and as a review-promoted case. coverageWarnings flags a brand imported with only ONE polarity — 40 genuine cases and no fakes scores perfectly and proves nothing, since the dangerous miss cannot occur; the mirror case (counterfeit-only) yields no false-positive rate, the error that harms sellers. Warnings do NOT reject, since a corpus may legitimately arrive in halves. Capped at 500 rows/batch. 4426 edge tests pass (+9). STILL THE BLOCKER: the labels themselves. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other.

userStories.title: Substantiation review of every public authenticity claim and its framing
userStories.description: Authenticity verdicts (likely_authentic / inconclusive / red_flags) are shown on public certificates and returned from an unauthenticated public endpoint, currently with no accuracy gate behind them. Separately, the seeded brand KB was written to REFUSE authentication — 00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql:14 reads 'NEVER auto-authenticate... A creed/serial proves NOTHING about authenticity on its own' — so our own knowledge base contradicts the product's public posture. That contradiction needs resolving deliberately, not by drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Review every user-facing authenticity string against what the evidence can actually support, with counsel — fold into the US-2114 review gate rather than running a separate process.

Decide and document the claim posture: assessment/opinion with stated limitations vs verification. The pipeline is built for the former (confidence ceilinged at 0.9, hard-capped to 0.5 on contradiction, limitations set from a constant the model cannot override) — keep that discipline in the copy.

userStories.title: Garment sellers are never asked for a serial or date-code photo
userStories.description: photo-profiles.ts:31-45 defines serial and marking slots but surfaces them ONLY for non-clothing profiles. A garment seller is never prompted for a date code, interior stamp, or hardware close-up — while ai-authenticity.ts:142-151 asks the model for stitch-per-inch, embroidery backing, screen-print registration and rivet engraving. The prompt requests evidence the capture flow never collects. This is the cheapest single improvement to authenticity signal quality.
acceptanceCriteria: Add serial/date-code and hardware/stamp macro slots to the clothing photo profile, surfaced when the authenticity add-on is active.
Make them optional-but-encouraged rather than blocking a condition grade — a grade must never fail because an authenticity slot was skipped.
Feed slot presence into the authenticity confidence: absent macro evidence should lower confidence and widen limitations, not be silently ignored.
Mirror across web and iOS (photo required-set and order surfaces change together — see the photo-required-and-order-surfaces memory; ~7 spots).
Update the prompt so it asks only for what the available slots can actually support.

userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). The server does no further resize, and Claude's own ~1568px normalization is the effective ceiling. A label filling a third of the frame yields roughly 500px of label: enough to OCR a size, nowhere near enough for stitch density, kerning, weave or engraving fidelity. The only real magnification path today is the Forensic add-on's defect zoom (grading-pipeline.ts:130-172), which crops the retained original and upscales to a 320px minimum — but it is keyed to defect bboxes only, never to tags or hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.
Generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching) rather than defect bboxes only — this is the most reusable existing asset.
Measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it, so confidence can be conditioned on real evidence quality rather than assumed.
Respect the existing storage/upload hardening path (validateImageUpload -> stripImageMetadata -> upload) and the Vision budget ceiling.
Do not raise resolution globally — the upload-speed tradeoff that motivated the iOS reduction is real; scope the increase to authenticity slots.

userStories.title: Deepen brand-decoders cross-checks — the strongest deterministic signal we have
userStories.description: brand-decoders.ts is a data-driven regex decoder engine whose crossCheck produces DecodeInconsistency on impossible dates (date_in_future, date_before_brand at :236-245), fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence (ai-authenticity.ts:346-353). This is deterministic contradiction detection — it does not depend on model judgment, cannot be talked out of a finding, and is already built and underused. It is the highest-confidence authenticity signal available today and the one most worth extending. CORRECTION 2026-07-19 (after reading vault/20-domain/brands/brand-kb-decoder-bar.md, which the grading-engine skill instructs be read BEFORE adding any decoder): this story as originally filed invites the exact failure that note forbids. Decoders must clear tag-printed AND regular AND BRAND-UNIQUE IN FORMAT, plus a fourth question added 2026-07-19 — WHICH ENTITY does the identifier name? Reebok, PUMA, Chanel/Moncler/Balenciaga serials, the Canada Goose hologram and URBN OB###### are all deliberately decoder-less; they look like coverage gaps and are not. Decoder authority OUTRANKS the AI on conflict, so a false decoder does not merely add a wrong guess — it overrides a correct one. Expanding coverage by submission volume, as originally written, would mint false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: Treat CROSS-CHECKS and DECODERS as different risk classes. A cross-check detects a contradiction (impossible date, mismatched era) and cannot mis-attribute a brand — that is the safe expansion path and where effort should go. A decoder RECOVERS a brand from a code and can override a correct read.
Any new decoder must clear all three bar tests AND the which-entity question, with the reasoning recorded in the vault note alongside the existing table.
Do NOT seed a decoder for any code listed as a deliberate refusal — extend the refusal table instead if a new one is evaluated and rejected.

A parent-wide or shared identifier (URBN OB######, shared RN 66170) can never attribute a sibling brand. Any RN/CA cross-check must handle shared RNs explicitly rather than treating RN -> brand as one-to-one.
Codes that fail the bar get transcribed into tag_eras or authentication_tells, never wired to brand recovery.
A contradiction from a deterministic decoder must dominate model optimism — verify applyVerdictCap composition holds (caps compose as a min and never raise).
Surface which decoders fired in the operator view so a verdict is explainable.

Deterministic signal is also the most defensible claim: 'the date code is impossible for this brand' is a fact, not an opinion. Prioritize this over model-side tuning. The safe, high-value work here is CROSS-CHECK expansion (contradiction detection), not decoder expansion (brand attribution) — the vault note is unambiguous that a false decoder is worse than no decoder. Read vault/20-domain/brands/{brand-kb-decoder-bar,brand-kb-alias-refusals,brand-kb-negative-findings}.md before touching this. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ THIS STORY'S FOUNDING PREMISE IS FALSE — READ BEFORE STARTING. The description states the cross-checks are 'fed into the prompt as trusted DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS outside the seller-input fence'. THEY ARE NOT. Traced end to end: buildTellsBlock (ai-authenticity.ts:386) accepts a crossChecks array and renders the DECODER_CROSS_CHECKS block, and assessAuthenticity reads it as `context.crossChecks ?? []` (:543) — but NOTHING IN THE CODEBASE EVER SUPPLIES IT. All four production callers (grading-pipeline.ts:1243, buyer-authenticity.ts:50, public-grading.ts:1106, authenticity-eval.ts:484) pass `{ tells }` only. So the array is always empty, the block never renders, and crossCheckDecodeResult — the only producer — has ZERO callers (found by audit-unwired-exports.mjs). THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS STORY: every AC is about DEEPENING a signal that is not connected. Adding decoders and cross-checks as written would extend a pure function whose output still reaches nothing, and the work would test green throughout — the deepened signal simply never reaches the model. WIRE IT FIRST, and note the plumbing already exists on the consuming side, so this is genuinely small: ai-extract.ts already computes decoderHits: DecodeResult[] (:946,:981) in production. The missing step is running crossCheckDecodeResult over those hits and passing the result as context.crossChecks. BUT IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER, and this is the part worth flagging: this ADDS DYNAMIC PER-ITEM CONTEXT TO AN AUTHENTICITY PROMPT, which the grading-engine skill requires be flag-gated and to SUFFIX prompt_version so accuracy tracking can attribute eras (the same rule that governs +baseline/+fabric/+visual). Shipping it unflagged would silently change verdicts under an unchanged version string and make every before/after accuracy comparison meaningless. AC6 (applyVerdictCap composition) also cannot be verified today, because a contradiction can never currently reach the model to dominate its optimism. RECOMMEND: split the wiring (+ flag + version suffix + eval) out as its own story ahead of this one; the decoder-bar discipline in AC2-AC5 is unaffected and still correct.

userStories.title: Per-brand tell depth is 3 brands and 7 tells, all unverified
userStories.description: CANONICAL_TELLS covers exactly three brands (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) with 7 tells total across categories date_code/stamp/hardware/serial/font — every one marked 'seed:brand-authentication-tells (unverified — review in admin)' at confidence 0.5-0.65, against a taxonomy of 11 categories that includes stitching, construction and material. The separate seeded brand_knowledge.authentication_tells rows are legacy {tell, detail} shape, coerced on read to category 'other' with NO redFlag field (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92), so they contribute almost nothing to the contradiction logic that drives the verdict. admin-brand-knowledge.ts is a working curation surface with validateTellsForWrite and is the right place to do this. EXTENDED 2026-07-19: the KB is also ONE-SIDED. Every field models what a GENUINE example looks like — authentication_tells, tag_eras, country_patterns, registered_numbers — and there is no counterfeit-pattern modelling at all: no known fake markers, no superfake characteristics, no record of a specific counterfeit production tell. authentication_tells is a single column marked 'informational' doing double duty for both directions. Combined with seeded content that says 'NEVER auto-authenticate', the KB currently argues against the product it feeds.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrate legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape so they can carry a category and a redFlag and actually affect the verdict.
Expand verified tells to the brands with real submission volume; mark provenance and confidence per tell.
Establish a review workflow so a tell moves from unverified to verified deliberately, with a named source.
Gate: a brand with no verified tells should widen limitations and lower confidence rather than producing a confident verdict from generic reasoning.

Model counterfeit-side knowledge distinctly from genuine-side tells — a known fake marker is a different kind of fact from 'what a real one looks like', and collapsing them into one informational column is why neither drives the verdict.
Reconcile the seeded 'NEVER auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture (see US-2133) rather than leaving the KB and the product in contradiction.

So AC1 is a SEPARATION job first: split identification knowledge out of authentication_tells, then categorize only what actually authenticates. userStories.title: human_reviews is condition-shaped — an authenticity review has nowhere to land
userStories.description: Authenticity already routes to human review correctly: authenticityNeedsReview() (ai-authenticity.ts:440) forces needs_human_review on a red_flags verdict or a branded assessment under 0.7 confidence, on an axis independent of condition confidence (grading-pipeline.ts:2087). But human_reviews (00003_admin_tables.sql:66) is shaped for condition grading — original_score/adjusted_score decimals — so a reviewer has no field to record an authenticity outcome in. The review is requested and then cannot be properly resolved.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an authenticity outcome model: the reviewer's verdict, their reasoning, which tells they relied on, and whether they overrode the model.
Resolved authenticity reviews must be able to feed the golden set — this is the cheapest ongoing source of labeled ground truth we have.
Keep condition and authenticity review outcomes distinguishable in the admin queue.
Follow the migrations skill (idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bump same commit, self-record footer) and the tenant-isolation skill for any new operator table.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Review][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. This closes the loop: reviews become training data, which feeds the golden set, which unblocks the gate. Sequencing-wise it pays for itself faster than any model tuning. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: migration 00487_authenticity_review_outcomes.sql (HELD — packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md, do not push until applied to prod) + services/edge-functions/src/lib/authenticity-review.ts. Separate table rather than columns on human_reviews: the two outcomes share no vocabulary (a grade correction is a number; an authenticity outcome is a verdict plus the tells it rested on), and separation is what lets the admin queue show them distinctly. Model verdict/confidence/prompt_version are SNAPSHOTTED so a later re-assessment cannot rewrite what the reviewer was looking at. overrodeModel maps between the two vocabularies before comparing and treats a null model verdict as NOT an override (the pass never ran, so there was nothing to disagree with — counting it would inflate the apparent error rate). isDangerousOverride isolates model-said-authentic/reviewer-said-fake, the same error the eval gate fails outright on. canPromoteToGoldenSet rejects inconclusive outcomes (a valid review result but a poor eval case — it cannot demonstrate the distinction the gate measures and inflates the agreement denominator), requires reasoning (an unexplained label cannot be audited), and refuses double promotion. 4367 edge tests pass (+10). STILL OPEN: the admin routes that write outcomes and perform the promotion, and the admin queue UI distinguishing the two review types. ITER7 2026-07-19: routes landed — POST /api/admin/grading/authenticity/reviews (upsert-by-report so a re-review corrects rather than stacks a second verdict; snapshots the model verdict; audits overrode_model and dangerous_override explicitly) and POST /authenticity/reviews/:id/promote (builds an eval case from the submission photos, tags it review_promoted, records source_url=internal:authenticity_review_outcome/<id> as provenance, and links back under an .is(golden_case_id,null) guard so a double-promote race cannot leave two cases behind one review). CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: nearly snapshotted grade_reports.image_authenticity (00061, PHOTO-EDIT detection) instead of authenticity_assessment (00172, the BRAND authenticity add-on) — different systems, and the prompt says so explicitly; that would have recorded a photo-manipulation score as the counterfeit verdict. Promotion refuses a submission with no brand, since brand_key joins brand_knowledge and per-brand regression is what blocks activation. 4367 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: the admin queue UI distinguishing the two review types (frontend). BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. | Verified closeable 2026-07-30. migration 00487 authenticity_review_outcomes (reviewer_verdict / tells_relied_on / reasoning / golden_case_id) applied to prod; admin record + promote route + separate admin surface shipped. All ACs met. VERIFIED.

GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. The selling point is real, but selling it ahead of the evidence is exactly the FTC Section 5 exposure the other batch is fixing. Sequence last.

userStories.title: PARKED: guarantee-backed authenticity — record the decision, fix the pool race first
userStories.description: A financial guarantee is what makes authentication commercially credible (Entrupy's model), but it is a categorically worse actuarial bet than the condition guarantee: a counterfeit claim is a total loss on item value rather than a fee refund, and fakes arrive in correlated batches from a single bad seller — precisely the shape a fixed period budget handles worst. The buyer-guarantee rails it would ride on also have two known flaws: the pool gate reads state BEFORE the insert while drawdown is recorded AFTER (buyer-guarantee-claim.ts:319 vs :357), so concurrent claims can both pass against the same pre-drawdown state; and credit-grant failure is swallowed with console.error (:366) while the claim already reads auto_approved and the pool is already drawn down.
acceptanceCriteria: Record the decision NOT to offer a guarantee-backed authenticity claim at this stage, with the reasoning, as a vault decision note under vault/60-decisions/.
Fix the pool drawdown race with a transactional reserve, and stop swallowing credit-grant failures — worth doing for the existing buyer guarantee regardless.
Define what would have to be true to revisit: gate pass rate, false-positive rate, per-brand coverage, and claim-severity modelling.
Do not implement an authenticity guarantee until those thresholds are met.

userStories.title: A seller whose GENUINE item is flagged has no way to contest it
userStories.description:
Every control in the authenticity module protects the buyer. There is nothing for a seller whose genuine item receives a red_flags verdict: the dispute system is grade/condition-shaped and carries no authenticity path (verified — zero authenticity references in the dispute routes/lib), there is no appeal, no re-assessment, and no way to have a wrong verdict withdrawn.

This got WORSE on 2026-07-19, by our own hand. US-2141 sealed the verdict into certificate integrity v4, and US-2142 wrote it to the garment passport — an append-only ledger with no update or delete policy. So a wrong verdict is now durable, tamper-evident, and by design cannot be erased. We made the record permanent before building the correction path.

Three things compound it: the pass has never cleared an accuracy gate (US-2130/2131), so we cannot state an error rate; confidence is capped but not zero when no macro evidence exists (US-2134), so thin-evidence verdicts still publish; and this is the error direction a financial guarantee would NOT cover (Entrupy-style guarantees pay out on fakes sold as real, not on genuine items called fake), so the seller bears it entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: A seller can contest an authenticity verdict from the surfaces where they see it, with a defined SLA and a human decision — not a form that goes nowhere.

Define what the certificate and passport show WHILE an appeal is open. The passport is append-only, so a withdrawal is a superseding event, never a deletion — decide and document what the public view renders for a superseded verdict.

Wire the outcome through the existing authenticity review path (US-2140) so an upheld appeal produces a reviewer verdict, and a wrongly-flagged genuine item becomes an 'authentic' golden-set case — the most valuable label we can get.
Reseal the certificate on withdrawal (integrity v4 covers the verdict, so a change without a reseal breaks verification).
Notify the seller when a red_flags verdict is published, not only when they happen to look. They cannot contest what they never saw.
Counsel sign-off on the notice and appeal wording — fold into US-2133 rather than running a separate review.
userStories.notes: [P0][Authenticity/Fairness][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Publicly attaching 'red flags' to a real person's item, from a model with no measured error rate, has a defamation-adjacent shape that belongs in the counsel review. Sharpest open exposure in the module. Sequence with US-2133; do not let an agent draft the notice language. PARTIAL 2026-07-19 (mechanics only): migration 00489 adds disputes.kind (grade|authenticity, default grade) — EXTENDING the existing disputes table rather than building an appeals table, since disputes is already generic at the schema level (grade_report_id, user_id, free-text reason, status, resolution_notes) and only its RESOLUTION path is grade-shaped. One lifecycle, one admin queue, one place a user looks. HELD; packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. lib/authenticity-appeal.ts encodes three decisions worth review: (1) an upheld appeal CLEARS the verdict rather than flipping it to likely_authentic — the assessment should never have been published, which is not the same as positively vouching for the item, and asserting that would be the same overreach reversed; (2) the reseal carries the SCORES through untouched, because an authenticity appeal says nothing about condition and silently re-deriving a grade would change a number nobody contested; (3) a REJECTED appeal produces NO golden-set case — upholding the original verdict is not a human independently confirming counterfeit (the reviewer may just have found the appeal unpersuasive), and treating it as ground truth would seed the golden set with unverified labels. An upheld appeal DOES yield an authentic case, which is a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE — the most valuable label available, and the error direction US-2146 exists to measure. 4408 edge tests pass (+7). DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED, still needs you + counsel (US-2133): what the certificate and passport RENDER while an appeal is open, the SLA, the seller notification wording, and whether a published red_flags verdict should notify the seller proactively. No routes shipped yet — the lib is pure logic + tests, so nothing is user-reachable until those decisions land. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (in my own iteration-4 work): withdrawAssessment cleared only verdict/verdict_confidence, but the PUBLIC certificate view (00172, carried through 00307) does NOT read verdict — it derives what a buyer sees from authenticity_confidence (-> confidence band), counterfeit_risk (-> risk label) and summary (rendered verbatim). So an upheld appeal would have cleared the internal verdict while the certificate kept publicly showing an elevated counterfeit risk and the original red-flag summary: the seller wins and stays flagged, which is exactly the failure this story exists to fix. Now clears every projected field, moves the original under withdrawn_original (operator-side; no view projects it) so the record of what was said survives, and exports PUBLICLY_PROJECTED_ASSESSMENT_FIELDS with a test that iterates it — if the view ever learns a new field, that test fails rather than a seller silently staying flagged. Also confirmed: the edge-SSR cert page renders no authenticity at all (SPA-only), and authenticity_checked in the public view derives from image_authenticity (PHOTO-EDIT, 00061), which is a different signal from the brand add-on and must not be conflated. 4412 edge tests pass. SELLER ROUTE 2026-07-19: POST /api/grade/authenticity-appeal shipped, implementing the approved §1a/§1b decisions. Files as disputes.kind=authenticity (00489) rather than a parallel table. Ownership verified through the submission (grade_reports has no user_id) and a miss reports 404 so an id probe cannot distinguish does-not-exist from not-yours; viewers are blocked, matching the grade-dispute route. Hiding the verdict while an appeal is open is REVERSIBLE — hideAssessmentForAppeal clears the publicly-projected fields and stashes the originals under appeal_hidden_original, so a rejected appeal restores exactly what was there and hiding is not a quiet way to lose a verdict; hiding twice does not bury the original (tested). Rate limited to 5 open appeals per seller, which exists BECAUSE hiding is free otherwise: unlimited appeals would suppress every verdict indefinitely at no cost. CAUGHT DURING IMPLEMENTATION: the first version called the reseal before the update landed, so it would have hashed the OLD verdict and written a signature verifying against nothing — resealAfterAuthenticityChange now takes the NEXT assessment explicitly, which makes that mistake impossible rather than merely fixed. If hiding fails the appeal is still recorded (better a visible verdict with a filed appeal than a silent appeal nobody actions). 4431 edge tests pass. STILL OPEN: the admin resolve route, seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (needs the SLA number + counsel). ADMIN RESOLVE 2026-07-19: GET /authenticity/appeals (open queue, OLDEST FIRST — while an appeal is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade, so waiting time is itself a penalty) + POST /authenticity/appeals/:id/resolve. Step-up gated: upholding withdraws a published verdict and reseals a certificate, rejecting republishes one. Upheld -> withdrawAssessment (permanent, clears every publicly-projected field); rejected -> restoreAssessmentAfterAppeal (exactly what was hidden, since the reviewer finding the appeal unpersuasive is not a new finding about the item). Both reseal with the NEXT assessment. An upheld appeal also records an authentic reviewer verdict through the US-2140 path, because a confirmed FALSE POSITIVE is the most valuable label available and the error direction nothing else measures — the model_verdict snapshot reads from appeal_hidden_original, since the live field was nulled when the appeal was filed. Already-resolved appeals 409 rather than double-applying. 4431 edge tests pass. REMAINING on this story: seller notification on a published red_flags verdict, and the notice wording (SLA number + counsel). | 2026-07-19 ⚠ STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — do not act on it. The migration(s) this note calls HELD (00061, 00172, 00307, 00489) are all on origin/main, verified individually with git log origin/main against each file rather than inferred from the linter's summary. The standing rule makes this decisive: a commit containing a migration is NOT pushed until the operator has applied the SQL, so a migration present on origin/main was pushed, which means its hold was already released. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md agrees — every entry through 00490 (the highest migration in the tree) is marked APPLIED and confirmed by the user, so nothing is genuinely pending. WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO CORRECT: a stale hold tells the next reader the branch is frozen when it is not, which either invites a pointless prod session or — worse — makes them hold back an unrelated push that was always safe. Correction APPENDED rather than edited into the original sentence, because these notes are append-only and the history of what was believed when is itself worth keeping. NOTIFICATION 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-notify.ts, fired from the pipeline at finalize. Implements the approved §1a decision — red_flags ONLY, never on inconclusive (not a finding; telling a seller invites appeals against nothing) and never on likely_authentic. SLA of 5 business days is stated in the notice, per the decision: an appeal with no stated turnaround cannot be planned around, and while it is open the item is effectively unsellable at its stated grade. COPY IS DELIBERATELY NON-ACCUSATORY and tested to stay that way — it says the check flagged details it COULD NOT CONFIRM, calls itself an automated photo estimate and not a determination, and a test asserts the words counterfeit/fake never appear, because the pass has no measured error rate and must not assert what it cannot support. Rides the existing dispute_update channel rather than inventing a type the users notification preferences do not know about, which would have made it unsuppressable. Best-effort so a notification problem never breaks a paid grade. ⚠ COPY STILL NEEDS COUNSEL REVIEW under US-2133 — flagged in the module header; it should be reviewed alongside the certificate copy, not separately. 4453 edge tests pass (+22).

userStories.title: No accuracy tracking for authenticity — zero drift detection
userStories.description:
accuracy-tracking.ts contains ZERO references to authenticity (verified). Grading has per-era accuracy attribution keyed on prompt_version; authenticity has none. The eval gate (US-2130) is a point-in-time certification — it says a prompt version cleared a bar on a given day. Nothing tells us it is still true a month later, after a model change, a brand-mix shift, or a prompt-version suffix change.

The inputs now exist and are going unused: US-2140 records reviewer verdicts against model verdicts with overrode_model and dangerous_override already derived, and US-2142 stamps every passport event with prompt_version and gate state.
acceptanceCriteria: Track authenticity outcomes over time, attributed by prompt_version (mirroring how grading attributes accuracy eras).
Surface verdict distribution, override rate, and DANGEROUS-override rate specifically — the last is the metric that matters, since it is the error the gate fails outright on.
Alert on drift rather than requiring someone to look: a rising dangerous-override rate is the signal that a passing gate has gone stale.
Slice per brand, so a regression confined to one brand is visible (per-brand regression is what blocks activation).
Feed from the review outcomes recorded in US-2140 rather than standing up a parallel data path.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Monitoring][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Only becomes meaningful once the gate can pass (US-2131), but the data is already accumulating — build it before there is a year of unattributed history to backfill. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-accuracy.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/accuracy?since=ISO. The central design decision is that the TWO ERROR DIRECTIONS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE and are never collapsed into one accuracy number: a FALSE NEGATIVE (model said likely_authentic, human confirmed counterfeit) means a buyer got a fake we vouched for — the error the eval gate fails outright on and the one a guarantee would pay out against; a FALSE POSITIVE (model said red_flags, human confirmed authentic) means a seller genuine item was publicly flagged, which nobody reimburses and which US-2145 has no correction path for. Drift is judged on those two rates, NOT on agreement — tested with the case that motivates the whole module: a window where agreement is byte-identical to baseline while the version stopped missing fakes and started flagging genuine items, which is much worse and completely invisible in an agreement rate. Drift refuses to fire below MIN_DRIFT_SAMPLE in each window (a gate declared stale on four reviews is noise, and a monitor that cries wolf gets muted). Attribution is per prompt_version and per brand, mirroring how grading attributes accuracy eras; reviews of items the pass never assessed are excluded rather than dragging every rate. 4401 edge tests pass (+10). STILL OPEN: alerting (currently pull-only via the route), and the operator UI. NOTE the false-positive rate this computes is exactly the measured number vault/60-decisions/adr-authenticity-guarantee.md names as revisit criterion 2. ITER5 2026-07-19: closed the alerting AC. checkAuthenticityDrift fires when a review outcome is RECORDED, not from a cron — two reasons: a review is the only thing that can move these rates, so a write is exactly when the answer can change (a schedule would mostly recompute an unchanged result), and the cron fleet is a manual per-environment install, so a scheduled check is one an operator must remember to enable before it ever protects anything (72 crons are already uninstalled per US-1566). Reviews are human-gated and low-volume, so per-write recomputation is affordable in a way it would not be on a hot path. Rates are emitted on EVERY check so a dashboard has a continuous series even when healthy; the drift_detected metric + warning fire only on an actual regression. Tested that a monitoring failure returns null and never fails the write it observes. The accuracy route and the drift check now share loadAuthenticityObservations, so the number an operator reads and the number that alerts cannot disagree. 4411 edge tests pass (+3). BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Consequences were real in all three: golden-set cases filed under keys nothing reads (so per-brand coverage, which is what blocks activation, read thinner than reality); tell candidates an operator would promote into a key nothing reads; and per-brand accuracy splitting one brand across its spellings, diluting exactly the per-brand regression it exists to detect. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other. | Verified closeable 2026-07-30 (code-complete, no operator tail). authenticity-accuracy.ts computeAuthenticityAccuracy (by prompt_version+brand) + checkAuthenticityDrift emits an alert on each new review; admin /admin/authenticity surface shipped; migration 00487 applied (<=00503 = live in prod). All ACs met in code. VERIFIED.

userStories.title: Reviewer tells never flow back into brand knowledge — the loop is half-built
userStories.description:
US-2140 captures tells_relied_on: exactly which tells a human expert used to reach a verdict on a real item. That is the highest-value authenticity data the system can generate, and nothing aggregates it. It flows into the golden set as a single eval case and stops there — it never reaches brand_knowledge.authentication_tells or CANONICAL_TELLS, which are what ground future assessments.

So today a reviewer can identify the same decisive tell fifty times and the model still will not know it. Closing this converts every human review into permanent, reusable brand knowledge instead of one test case.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregate tells_relied_on per brand and surface candidates in the admin brand-knowledge curation surface (admin-brand-knowledge.ts already exists with validateTellsForWrite).
PROPOSE, never auto-promote: a tell entering the KB changes future verdicts, so it needs the same deliberate review a seeded tell gets. Frequency is evidence, not authority.
Carry provenance — which reviews supported the tell, and how often it was decisive vs merely noted.
Respect the vault's brand rules before writing anything: read vault/20-domain/brands/ (the decoder bar, the alias refusals, the negative findings) — several absences there are deliberate.

Migrate the legacy {tell, detail} rows into the structured shape as part of this, or aggregated tells will land in a field that contributes nothing to the verdict (brand-authenticity.ts:88-92 coerces them to category 'other' with no redFlag).
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Knowledge][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Cheap and compounding — it wires two systems that already exist. Overlaps US-2139 (tell depth); do them together, since this is the mechanism that makes US-2139 self-sustaining rather than a one-off curation push. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/tell-candidates.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/tell-candidates. Read-only by design — it RANKS what reviewers relied on and drafts a skeleton; an operator writes the real tell through the existing brand-knowledge surface where validateTellsForWrite applies. Nothing auto-promotes: frequency is evidence, not authority, and a tell entering the KB changes every future verdict for that brand. Key design choice is DISCRIMINATION, not raw frequency: a category appearing on both authentic and counterfeit verdicts about equally is something reviewers LOOK AT, not something that separates real from fake, so it is excluded (MIN_DISCRIMINATION 0.7) — seeding it would add noise to every verdict. Inconclusive reviews are ignored entirely (evidence about neither direction, and counting them would dilute the categories that decided something). Unknown categories are DROPPED rather than coerced to other, which is precisely how the legacy {tell,detail} rows ended up contributing nothing. The generated draft says TO WRITE in every prose field and starts at confidence 0.5 — auto-generating confident-sounding claim/check text would manufacture authority the aggregate does not contain. Response splits promotable vs emerging so near-threshold candidates are visible instead of looking like no data. 4384 edge tests pass (+8). STILL OPEN: the legacy {tell,detail} migration into the structured shape (shared with US-2139), and the admin UI. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): brand_key was derived as brandKey(rawBrand) in three places I wrote, skipping alias resolution. The canonical path is brandKey(canonicalizeBrand(raw)) — as getEffectiveTellsForBrand does — so a seller writing "Levi Strauss" keyed as levistrauss while the KB row is levis, and "Blue Bell" (the pre-1986 parent mark that IS a Wrangler) keyed as bluebell. The two never join, and the failure is INVISIBLE: a lookup that finds nothing looks exactly like a brand we have no knowledge of. Fixed with a single exported brandKeyForRaw() in brand-normalize.ts (one derivation, not three copies), callers now DROP an unresolvable brand rather than bucketing it under "", and four regression tests pin the alias behaviour. FOLLOW-UP 2026-07-19 (self-audit): tells_relied_on was accepted as any string array on write while the aggregator DROPS anything that is not a known AuthTellCategory — so a reviewer could record free-text tells, see a 201, and have the signal silently vanish at aggregation. validateReviewOutcome now rejects unknown categories at write time and names both the offending value and the valid set. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other. | SCOPED 2026-07-30, AC5 NOT ATTEMPTED — deliberately, because the obvious version of it is a regression. Measured the corpus: 179 legacy payload arrays holding 599 individual {tell,detail} entries across the 37 *_brand_knowledge.sql seeds; structured payloads = 0. Two findings that change what AC5 is. (1) A BULK CATEGORIZATION WOULD SILENTLY REMOVE A PAID DISCLOSURE. authenticity-coverage.ts:53 isActionableTell returns true when category !== 'other' OR redFlag is set, so assigning categories alone flips every one of those 179 packs from 'inert' to 'actionable' — which lifts coverageConfidenceCap from COVERAGE_CAP_INERT 0.75 to 1.0 and empties the limitations string the PURCHASED add-on owes its buyer (US-2219 shipped that cap precisely because these rows cannot move a verdict). Not one new verified fact would have been added. That is a user-visible regression on a paid product, dressed as a data migration. (2) MOST OF THE 599 ARE NOT AUTHENTICATION TELLS AT ALL — the column is doing double duty as general brand knowledge. Real examples from the seeds: 'American Eagle runs LARGE', 'Anthropologie also SELLS other brands', 'PINK IS NOT VICTORIA'S SECRET — comp it separately', 'AERIE IS AMERICAN EAGLE — and the tag does not say so'. All 599 are injected into the <<<KNOWN_AUTHENTICATION_TELLS>>> block (ai-authenticity.ts:409-422) under the instruction 'check the item against EACH and report a finding per tell', capped at MAX_TELLS 60 per brand — so sizing and comping rules both generate noise findings and can crowd out real tells. The reshape is therefore a SEPARATION problem first (identification vs authentication knowledge) and a categorization problem second; doing the second without the first is what makes it harmful. AC5 is the SAME work as US-2139 AC1, and authenticity-coverage.ts:20 already names US-2139 as its owner ('Re-shaping the legacy rows is US-2139's job'). Recommend deleting AC5 from this story as a duplicate and carrying it only on US-2139, where the counterfeit-side modelling (US-2139 AC5) that a real redFlag needs also lives. Already guarded, so nobody can do this silently: authenticity-coverage_test.ts:201 asserts structured payloads == 0 and tells the next author to update the floor rather than delete the test. userStories.title: Nothing aggregates authenticity outcomes per seller (reputation route was wrong)
userStories.description:
reputation_events + computeTrustScore + resolveReputationPerks are built (US-1816/1817), and a CONFIRMED counterfeit is the strongest reputation signal the platform could have. Nothing emits it — verified: no emitReputationEvent call anywhere in ai-authenticity.ts or the grading pipeline.

There is also no seller-level aggregation of authenticity outcomes at all. Three red_flags verdicts across one seller's items is invisible, and that is precisely the correlated-batch pattern vault/60-decisions/adr-authenticity-guarantee.md identifies as the shape our claims budget handles worst. CORRECTION 2026-07-19: this story originally said to emit via emitReputationEvent + recomputeTrustScore. That is WRONG and would have caused real damage. reputation_events / buyer_trust_scores is explicitly the BUYER Trust Score (00417 header: "US-1816: buyer Trust Score"), and the perks it drives are buyer-side — guarantee-window bonus days and a reward multiplier (buyer-reputation-perks.ts). A seller who ships a counterfeit is a different subject entirely. Routing seller conduct into that log would conflate "do you file honest claims and confirm grades" with "do you sell fakes", and would express a seller penalty as a buyer perk change, which is meaningless. It would also pollute an event log whose stated authority is buyer behaviour, and require extending a CHECK constraint kept in deliberate lockstep with ReputationEventType.
acceptanceCriteria: Aggregate authenticity outcomes per SELLER for operator visibility — counts by verdict, human-confirmed counterfeits, and recency.

Surface CLUSTERING, not just totals: the risk shape the guarantee ADR names is a correlated batch from one seller, so several flags in a short window matters more than the same count spread over a year.

Base any seller-adverse signal on a HUMAN-CONFIRMED outcome (US-2140), never a raw model verdict — the pass has no measured error rate, and an automated penalty off an ungated verdict is US-2145 with consequences attached.
Do NOT write into reputation_events / buyer_trust_scores. If a seller-standing score is ever wanted it needs its own model; that is a separate product decision, not an extension of the buyer epic.
Feed the seller-level signal into the guarantee correlated-batch risk per vault/60-decisions/adr-authenticity-guarantee.md.
userStories.notes: [P2][Authenticity/Reputation][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 reviewing the authenticity module for gaps after the epic's backend landed. Gated on US-2140's review path being in use, since the trigger must be a confirmed outcome rather than a model verdict. Note the asymmetry deliberately encoded in AC1: we penalise only what a human confirmed, but we may credit on either. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: lib/authenticity-seller-signal.ts + GET /api/admin/grading/authenticity/sellers. Deliberately does NOT touch reputation_events (see the correction on this story). The load-bearing output is CLUSTERING, not totals: peakClusterSize slides a 30-day window over CONFIRMED counterfeits, so three in five days ranks above four spread across a year — the batch signature the guarantee ADR names as the shape our claims budget handles worst. A sliding window rather than calendar buckets, since a fixed bucket would split a batch across a month boundary and miss exactly the case this exists to catch (tested). Model verdicts are counted but NEVER feed the cluster, so an ungated pass cannot manufacture a batch signature on its own. confirmed_authentic is tracked too, so a seller is not judged purely on model output — a human clearing a flagged item is evidence the flag was a false alarm. 4391 edge tests pass (+7). STILL OPEN: feeding the signal into the guarantee risk path, and the operator UI. VERIFIED CLEAN 2026-07-19 (self-audit): checked whether submissions.user_id is the right seller granularity under workspace ownership. It is — grade.ts writes user_id: ownerId where ownerId = workspaceOwnerId ?? userId, so a team member submission already attributes to the workspace owner. No change needed; recorded so it is not re-investigated. BUGFIX 2026-07-19 (self-audit): all three authenticity aggregate queries had unsafe caps. A limit with no ORDER BY is not a cap, it is an arbitrary sample — Postgres may return any 5000 rows, so recent-vs-baseline drift would be computed over a set that changes between calls. Worse, the tell-candidates query limited ONLY when a brand filter was supplied, leaving the LARGER unfiltered read unbounded. All three now order newest-first before limiting (so a capped read keeps the recent window intact — the part drift and clustering are actually about), share one AUTHENTICITY_AGGREGATE_CAP, and log when the cap bites. Same silent-truncation class as the certificate sitemap that quietly stopped at its first API page: a truncated aggregate reads as complete. UI 2026-07-19: /admin/authenticity console shipped (src/pages/admin/authenticity.tsx), route + nav registered. Gate status is the FIRST thing on the page rather than three clicks deep, because an ungated prompt is currently serving real users including a public endpoint. Accuracy NEVER renders a single number — the two error directions sit side by side and are labelled by WHO they harm (buyer got a fake we vouched for / seller had a genuine item flagged, which nobody reimburses), because a combined figure stays flat while a version trades one for the other. | Done 2026-07-30. AC5 SHIPPED, closing the story. lib/buyer-guarantee-claim.ts:evaluateSellerBatchRisk resolves the seller behind a claim's grade_report_id (grade_reports -> submissions.user_id) and counts human-confirmed counterfeits in the trailing CLUSTER_WINDOW_DAYS; lib/authenticity-seller-signal.ts:correlatedBatchHold is the pure decision, reusing the console's CLUSTER_THRESHOLD so an operator triaging a hold sees the number that caused it. fileBuyerGuaranteeClaim gathers it concurrently with evaluateClaimFraud and holds to manual_review BEFORE reservePoolDrawdown - that ordering is the whole point, since the ADR's flaw #2 is that the breaker trips AFTER the batch has drawn down. Four constraints, each deliberate: (1) NOT folded into fraud_flags - those signals are about the CLAIMANT and are retained for dispute defense, and a buyer who bought from a bad seller is not a suspicious buyer; filing seller conduct there is the same subject-conflation this story's own CORRECTION exists to prevent. (2) The buyer-visible decision_reason is opaque ('correlated_batch_review') because the buyer owns and can read the claim row, and a count would disclose how many confirmed counterfeits ANOTHER user has; the count reaches operators via the guarantee.seller_batch_hold metric instead. (3) reviewer_verdict='counterfeit' only, never a model verdict (AC3). (4) Fails open via captureException - an unresolvable seller or a failed query must not block a payout on a signal we did not actually read. Clustering clock is the report's created_at, not reviewed_at: a reviewer clearing a backlog in one afternoon would manufacture a batch signature out of our own queue latency. Vault same-commit: adr-authenticity-guarantee.md records the mitigation AND its limits (does not resize the pool; blind to a seller's first batch, which is every new bad seller), and two stale claims were corrected - both 'flaws to fix regardless' were already fixed by US-2144, which also satisfies revisit criterion 4; criteria 1-3 remain unmet so the park stands. Verified: deno check + deno lint clean, 22 affected edge tests pass (+6), negative-verified by planting an exclusive window boundary and a threshold off-by-one, each reddening exactly its own test, both reverted. Commit 177e531a. NOTE: 3 edge tests fail on main independently of this work (authenticity-references_test.ts US-2218 bucket assertion, sizing-chart-parity_test.ts US-2214/US-2215) - confirmed pre-existing by stashing this change and re-running.
