userStories.title: iOS tells capped sellers to slow down instead of upgrade (EdgeAPIError)
userStories.description: As an iOS seller who has used my monthly free Snap-to-Value allowance, I am told what actually happened and how to lift it, instead of being told to try again in a moment.
acceptanceCriteria: EdgeAPIError.from(statusCode:body:) maps any body carrying action:"upgrade" to a new upgrade-required case, keyed on the discriminator rather than the status — mirrors the Android US-1335 fix in EdgeApiError.kt
The case is checked AFTER the specific discriminators (workspace_access_revoked, email_unverified, feature_unavailable, offer_not_open) so a revoked workspace still recovers under the personal tenant
errorDescription surfaces the server sentence verbatim; the Snap and AI-enrichment call sites offer an upgrade route rather than a retry
The error is NOT retried (today the 429 → .rateLimited mapping retries a cap-reached snap twice, burning the per-IP daily ceiling)
Unit test covers both live sites: grade.ts snap cap (429, SNAP_LIMIT_REACHED / SNAP_IP_LIMIT_REACHED) and flipdesk-ai.ts enrichment-off (403)
userStories.notes: [P2][iOS/Networking] Found while porting Snap-to-Value for US-1335. Three edge sites emit action:"upgrade" (grade.ts:1020, grade.ts:1038, flipdesk-ai.ts:118) and iOS maps all three by status alone: the 429s become .rateLimited ("You are going a little too fast" — to someone who must wait until next month) and the 403 becomes .unauthorized ("Your session expired. Sign in again" — for a setting that is switched off). The server already writes the correct sentence in every case; only the client discards it. Android now keys on action:"upgrade"; this ports the same mapping so the two clients do not word the same state differently. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h), awaiting iOS CI (macOS) to validate — Swift cannot be compiled in this Linux sandbox. AC1: added EdgeAPIError.upgradeRequired(detail:code:) + WirePayload.action; from() maps any body with action:'upgrade' to it, mirroring Android EdgeApiError.kt (US-1335). AC2: the action check sits AFTER workspace_access_revoked / email_unverified / feature_unavailable/reconnect_required / offer_not_open and BEFORE the status switch (test_from_specificDiscriminator_winsOverUpgradeAction proves a revoked-workspace body that also carries action:upgrade still maps to .workspaceAccessRevoked). AC3: errorDescription returns the server sentence verbatim; the Snap call site (SnapStore.isUpgradePrompt + SnapView.errorCard) now shows an 'Upgrade' button opening PaywallView instead of 'Try again'. Enrichment site: the central mapping fix already surfaces the server's actionable 'AI enrichment is turned off… Enable it in Settings' verbatim (was the misleading 'session expired') and no longer retries — the route is named in the message (enrichment recovery is a Settings toggle, not the paywall); a dedicated button there would need threading isUpgradePrompt through AIExtractStore's .failed phase + AIExtractView (multi-file, uncompilable here) for marginal gain, so it is intentionally scoped out. AC4 (the real bug): the retry loop in EdgeAPI.swift intercepted a 429 by STATUS and threw .rateLimited BEFORE from() ran, so a cap-reached snap was retried twice (burning the per-IP daily ceiling). Restructured so from() runs first and only a genuine .rateLimited gets the Retry-After enrichment; .upgradeRequired is neither transient nor in shouldRetry, so it is not retried (test_snapCap429_action_upgrade_isNotRetried asserts calls.count==1). AC5: EdgeAPITests.swift covers all three live bodies — grade.ts 429 SNAP_LIMIT_REACHED + SNAP_IP_LIMIT_REACHED, flipdesk-ai.ts 403 enrichment-off (no code) — plus description-verbatim, isUpgradePrompt, discriminator-precedence, and the not-retried integration case. Verified in-sandbox: no exhaustive switch over EdgeAPIError lacks a default (checked EbayPublishService/FriendlyErrorCopy/EdgeAPI), so the new case breaks no call site; ios/Scripts/no-ungated-print.py clean. KEPT passes:false until iOS CI (macOS) is green on the branch.

userStories.title: Grade disputes have no server-side window and no duplicate gate
userStories.description: As the grading team, the dispute rules we advertise are actually enforced, so the review queue reflects one complaint per grade and the filing window means something.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/grade/dispute rejects a filing for a grade report older than the window (currently 7 days, enforced only in client UI) with a typed, actionable error

A second dispute for the same (user_id, grade_report_id) is refused rather than inserted — today every client-side gate is advisory and a double-tap, a race between two devices, or a direct API call all create duplicate rows
Add the matching UNIQUE (user_id, grade_report_id) constraint to public.disputes (00001 created it without one; the UNIQUE in 00418 is on the unrelated buyer_purchases table)
Decide and document the canonical window in one place both clients read, so web / iOS / Android cannot drift again
Existing duplicate dispute rows are identified before the constraint is added, so the migration cannot fail on live data
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Edge] Found while porting the dispute flow for US-1340. The 7-day window lives in TWO client files with no server check, and the /dispute route inserts unconditionally: it verifies ownership and evidence but never looks for an existing dispute or at the report age. So the window is advisory and the re-file gate is cosmetic. Low severity today because filing is a UI action, but the duplicate case is reachable by an ordinary double-tap on a slow connection, and duplicates land in a human reviewer queue. The Android client (US-1340) gates on both client-side, matching web and iOS. | 2026-07-23 CODE COMPLETE (branch claude/session-planning-jokq5h), migration HELD for prod apply. AC1 (window): POST /api/grade/dispute now rejects a filing for a report older than DISPUTE_WINDOW_DAYS (7) with a typed 422 { code:'DISPUTE_WINDOW_EXPIRED', windowDays } (grade.ts) — previously only client UI checked age. AC2 (duplicate): the route SELECTs for an existing kind='grade' dispute on (ownerId, gradeReportId) and refuses with a 409 { code:'DISPUTE_ALREADY_EXISTS' }; a raced insert that beats the SELECT is caught via the 23505 unique-violation and returned as the same 409 instead of a 500. AC3 (constraint) + AC5 (dedup): migration 00493 deletes pre-existing duplicate grade disputes (keep earliest per user_id,grade_report_id) THEN builds the unique index, so it cannot fail on live data. DEVIATION FROM LITERAL AC3, documented: used a PARTIAL unique index on (user_id, grade_report_id) WHERE kind='grade', NOT the blanket UNIQUE the AC names — AC3 predates the kind column (00489); a blanket constraint would wrongly block a grade dispute and an authenticity appeal from coexisting on one report, and the authenticity path is deliberately re-fileable so it is left untouched. AC4 (canonical window): the SERVER is now the source of truth and echoes windowDays in the rejection; web inline '7' replaced by DISPUTE_WINDOW_DAYS in src/lib/constants.ts (used by submission-detail.tsx), and ios/GradeThread/Grading/DisputeReason.swift's GradeDisputeWindow.days comment now states the server enforces + is authoritative. Verified in-sandbox: web tsc -b clean (pinned TS 5.9.3; the env's TS 6.0.2 trips a pre-existing baseUrl-deprecation error unrelated to this change) + eslint clean on touched files. Deno not installed in this sandbox so the edge change was NOT deno-checked here — CI (deno lane) + verify:db (Docker, runs 00493 on a fresh schema) cover it. KEPT passes:false: 00493 is a HELD migration (packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md) — the duplicate gate is only race-proof once the index exists in prod. Flip to true after the SQL is applied (apply-prod-migrations.sh) + NOTIFY pgrst + edge redeploy. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-07-29: the HELD-migration claim above is STALE and should not be acted on. Every migration this story names is on origin/main and applied to prod (schema at 00503); PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is empty and the branch is not frozen. | Verified closeable 2026-07-30. routes/grade.ts /dispute enforces DISPUTE_WINDOW_DAYS (7d) and refuses a second grade dispute; migration 00493 (partial-unique + dedup) applied to prod. All ACs met in code. VERIFIED.

Analytics: Listing Performance + Community Insights fold into the existing analytics tab set
Sourcing: ScoutAI + Buy Decision + Sources + Buyer Demand become one route with in-page tabs
Old routes redirect to the canonical route + ?tab= so deep links, the command palette and flipdesk-search keep working
The US-1121 nav-contract comment in sidebar.tsx is updated to describe the new redirects
FlipDesk sidebar entries drop from ~24 to ~14 with no feature removed

userStories.title: End Listing on a non-eBay listing ends it only locally — the listing stays live and purchasable
userStories.description: As a reseller cross-listing beyond eBay, I want End to actually end the listing on its own marketplace, so FlipDesk never tells me an item is ended while buyers can still buy it.
acceptanceCriteria: endListing() in src/pages/flipdesk/listings.tsx branches on the LISTING'S platform, not on whether an eBay connection exists
A non-eBay listing is ended through its own adapter (MarketplaceAdapter.end) — never by a direct listings.update() from the browser
A platform with no server-side delist API (poshmark/mercari/grailed) stamps delist_requested_at so the Lister extension queue picks it up, exactly as autoEndCrossListings does
A platform we genuinely cannot end surfaces an explicit warning naming the marketplace — never the bare 'Listing ended locally.' toast
The 409 fallback path can no longer reach a silent local-only write: every branch either ends upstream, queues, or warns
A test covers: Shopify listing + eBay connection present → the eBay price/end endpoint is NOT called with a Shopify listing id
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Listings] Found during the 2026-07-25 listings-management deep dive. listings.tsx:1382 gates on `ebayConnection` rather than the row's platform; the eBay endpoint 409s at flipdesk-ebay.ts:4747 (no platform_offer_id on a non-eBay row), the catch falls through to a direct listings.update({listing_status:'ended'}) and toasts 'Listing ended locally.' Same bug class as US-1877 (prefilling is not publishing) from the other side. Oversell hazard. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. endListing() and bulkEndListings() in listings.tsx now call the US-2166 agnostic routes and have NO local-write fallback — the branch that produced "Listing ended locally." is gone. The server marks a row ended only when the listing is genuinely not live; a refused delist returns an error and the row stays active, so an item still for sale keeps looking like it. unsupported_platform / not_connected get a 12-14s toast naming the marketplace, because those are the cases where the listing is still buyable. bulkEndListings also became ONE request (see US-2163 note on the rate limit).

userStories.title: Bulk price drop writes local-only for non-eBay listings and makes N sequential browser calls
userStories.description: As a reseller running a markdown across a selection, I want the new price to reach every listing's marketplace in one batched server call, so my local prices never diverge from the live ones and 200 listings don't mean 200 round trips.
acceptanceCriteria: bulkPriceDrop() posts ONE request to a platform-agnostic server endpoint instead of looping per listing from the browser
The server dispatches through resolveAdapter()/updateListing per row, reusing the 25-per-call chunking already in /listings/bulk-price-quantity
A listing whose marketplace could not be repriced is reported as FAILED, not as 'updated locally only' — the local listing_price is not advanced for it
Per-row success/failure comes back structured and the UI shows which listings failed and why
Progress is reported while the batch runs and the dialog is cancellable
A test asserts a mixed eBay + Shopify selection reprices both upstream and reports per-platform outcomes
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx:1420 loops one HTTP call per selected listing under setBusy() with no progress or cancel; the 409 path (non-eBay rows) silently writes the local listing_price and reports it as `remoteSkipped` → toast '(N updated locally only)'. A diverged local price then poisons margin/ROI math. The server already has the batched, adapter-driven path at flipdesk-ebay.ts:4802 (/listings/bulk-price-quantity) and 4948 (/listings/bulk-edit) — this story wires the UI to it. Depends on US-2165 for the route move. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. bulkPriceDrop() and the inline price edit now use POST /bulk-price and POST /:id/price. Three properties beyond the AC text: (1) ORDERING — the server pushes to the marketplace FIRST and writes listings.listing_price only on success, so there is no window where the local price leads the live one and no rollback that could itself fail; safe because every adapter takes price from its input when > 0 (shopify/etsy/depop all do "price > 0 ? price : row.listing_price") and the routes validate price > 0. (2) drop_pct is applied SERVER-side to each row current price, so the result cannot be computed from a stale render. (3) the old browser loop would have tripped the 30-req/60s rate limit on /api/flipdesk/listings/* around the 30th selected row, so large bulk actions were silently half-finishing — one request removes that entirely. 11 hook tests lock the contract (agnostic URL, throw-not-fallback, one-request-per-batch). | Review 2026-07-28 (verification pass, NOT closing). Confirmed genuinely met: AC1 (bulkPriceDrop posts one request to /api/flipdesk/listings/bulk-price — use-listing-lifecycle.test.ts 18 tests green), AC3 (server pushes upstream FIRST then writes local; refused row keeps marketplace price, flipdesk-listings.ts:1390-1410), AC4 (structured per-row RowResult surfaced in listings.tsx). Two ACs NOT met, so the story correctly stays open: AC2 as written wants '25-per-call chunking' but /bulk-price is deliberately SEQUENTIAL per row (documented eBay rate-limit rationale, :1318) — a defensible deviation but not the literal AC; AC5 (progress reported while the batch runs + cancellable dialog) is unmet — listings.tsx bulkPriceDrop runs under a blocking setBusy(true) spinner with no progress and no cancel. To close: either implement per-row progress + cancel (AC5) or amend AC2/AC5 to match the one-request design.

userStories.title: Etsy and Whatnot siblings never auto-end when the item sells elsewhere — silent oversell
userStories.description: As a reseller cross-listed on Etsy, I want my Etsy listing pulled when the garment sells on another channel, so the same physical item can't be sold twice.
acceptanceCriteria: delistMethodFor() resolves 'etsy' to a real API delist method, wired to setEtsyListingState (lib/etsy-api.ts) to inactivate the listing
autoEndCrossListings() calls the Etsy delist before marking the local row ended, matching the ebay/shopify/depop branches
The Etsy delist stays behind isEtsyEnabled() — a disabled connector degrades to the US-2165 explicit-unsupported path, never to a silent success
Whatnot is either wired the same way or explicitly recorded as unsupported-with-a-marker under US-1662, with the choice stated in the code comment
A cross-listing-sale test asserts an Etsy sibling is delisted upstream on a sibling sale, and that a disabled Etsy connector produces a marker rather than a clean 'ended'
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/CrossListing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. API_DELIST (lib/cross-listing-sale.ts:29) covers only ebay/shopify/depop and EXTENSION_DELIST_PLATFORMS covers poshmark/mercari/grailed, so etsy and whatnot fall to 'unsupported': autoEndCrossListings (lib/cross-listings.ts:140-175) marks the local row ended with NO upstream call and NO delist_requested_at stamp, so there is no queue entry and no seller-visible signal. Etsy is the cheap half — setEtsyListingState already exists at lib/etsy-api.ts:342. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25: etsy → "etsy_api" in API_DELIST; an etsy_api arm in the new attemptUpstreamDelist() dispatch calls setEtsyListingState(...,"inactive") behind isEtsyEnabled(), with a disabled/disconnected connector falling to the US-2165 unresolved marker rather than a silent end. whatnot stays deliberately unsupported (its listing path is 501 pending US-1662) and now takes the marker path. Tests: delistMethodFor(etsy) flipped to etsy_api, plus a new guard that every CROSS_LISTING_PLATFORMS entry has a delist channel or is a declared KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED gap. NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime).

userStories.title: An 'unsupported' delist silently reports success — it must leave a durable marker
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want any listing FlipDesk could not end upstream to stay visibly unresolved, so a marketplace we don't automate never looks handled when it isn't.
acceptanceCriteria: A delistMethodFor() result of 'unsupported' stamps a durable marker on the listing (platform_fields, following the US-1290 oversell_conflict shape) instead of a clean listing_status:'ended'
The marker fires one in-app notice naming the marketplace and the listing, idempotent against a duplicate order webhook or re-sync
The marker drives a badge on the listing card / row, like sync_drift and oversell_conflict already do
autoEndCrossListings' return count distinguishes ended-upstream from ended-locally-only so callers can't over-report
A test asserts an unknown platform produces a marker + notice and is NOT counted as ended
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/CrossListing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. The `unsupported` arm of lib/cross-listings.ts treats an unknown platform as job-done. This is the generalized guard behind US-2164: even once Etsy is wired, the next platform added to CROSS_LISTING_PLATFORMS without a delist path must fail loudly rather than silently. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. Scope note — the fix went WIDER than the AC text: the per-platform if-chain in autoEndCrossListings became a switch on delistMethodFor(), so a FAILED api delist (dropped connection, rejected call) now earns the marker too, not only an "unsupported" platform. That was the same silent-divergence bug on the eBay/Shopify/Depop paths, which previously console.warn-ed and marked the row ended. Benign failures are classified out via the existing isOfferAlreadyEndedError/isNoEbayConnectionError helpers so a stale-but-already-ended eBay row does not raise a false banner. A never-published draft resolves to nothing_live, not unresolved, so the badge stays meaningful. AC3 (the badge) required building the UI path from scratch: platform_fields.oversell_conflict had been stamped since US-1290 with ZERO frontend readers, so src/components/flipdesk/listing-alert-markers.tsx now renders BOTH markers and closes that gap too. Rendered via a new ListingAlertsSection on the item page that reads EVERY platform's listing — the other listing panels are all .eq(platform,"ebay") and would have hidden the Etsy case entirely. Frontend verified: tsc -b, eslint, 2587 vitest tests green. Edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime).

userStories.title: Platform-agnostic listing operations live under /api/flipdesk/ebay and half of them hardcode eBay
userStories.description: As a reseller on more than one marketplace, I want price, revise and end to work on any listing through its own adapter, so the operations I can perform don't depend on which namespace a route happened to be written in.
acceptanceCriteria: Single-listing price, revise and end move to flipdesk-listings.ts and dispatch through resolveAdapter()/updateListing()/end()
The hardcoded `platform: "ebay"` in the ebayOriginWriteLock calls is replaced by the row's real platform, so origin derivation is correct for non-eBay rows
The eBay-specific pieces (offer ids, markdown Sale overlays, promotions, aspects) stay in flipdesk-ebay.ts — only the platform-agnostic lifecycle moves
The old /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/* paths keep responding (delegating to the new handlers) so shipped iOS/Android clients and the extension don't break
/listings/bulk-edit moves alongside them — it is already adapter-driven and only its mount point is wrong
Every moved route has a tenant-isolation_test.ts case at its new path
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. /listings/:id/price (flipdesk-ebay.ts:4701), /listings/:id/revise (:5447) and DELETE /listings/:id (:6263) hardcode platform:'ebay' at the origin-lock call (e.g. :4729) while /listings/bulk-edit (:4948) is correctly adapter-driven — all four mounted under the eBay namespace. Unblocks US-2162 and US-2163, which both need a platform-agnostic lifecycle endpoint to call. Mind the shipped-client compatibility rule: iOS ships copies of these paths. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 as an ADDITIVE layer, not a move. New platform-agnostic routes in flipdesk-listings.ts: POST /:id/price, POST /:id/end, POST /bulk-price, POST /bulk-end — each dispatching on the row REAL platform (eBay keeps the cheap targeted updateOfferPrice / offer withdraw; everything else goes through the adapter). The eBay-namespaced routes were deliberately LEFT IN PLACE rather than relocated: shipped iOS/Android builds and the browser extension call those paths and cannot be redeployed, and moving 2000 lines of eBay-specific logic (markdown Sale overlays, promotions, aspects, origin locks) would have risked far more than it fixed. AC1 as written (move + delete) is therefore NOT met and should be read as superseded — revisit only when the mobile clients have aged out. The hardcoded platform:"ebay" origin-lock bug IS fixed on the new routes via originLockResponse(), which passes the row own platform. Four tenant-isolation cases added. Frontend verified; edge NOT verified locally (no Deno runtime).

userStories.title: useItemsFull loads the tenant's entire inventory, every column, on 11 surfaces
userStories.description: As a reseller with a real catalog, I want FlipDesk pages to fetch only the rows and columns they render, so the app doesn't slow to a crawl as my inventory grows.
acceptanceCriteria: useItemsFull accepts an explicit column projection and a range/limit; `select("*")` with no bound is gone
Each of the 11 consumers declares the columns it actually reads
Surfaces that render a page of rows request that page server-side; surfaces that aggregate use a server-side aggregate rather than pulling rows to count them
The shared-cache-key hazard called out in the US-419 comment in listings.tsx is preserved: a narrower projection can never win a cache entry a wider consumer depends on
A guard test fails if an unbounded select on items_full is reintroduced
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/hooks/use-items-full.ts:52 is `.select("*").order("created_at")` with no range or limit, consumed by overview, pipeline, prep, grid, listings, item, composer, reconciliation and three components. Overlaps US-2023 (inventory.tsx paginates then loads everything anyway) — fold that story in or sequence them together. STILL OPEN as of 2026-07-25, but its blast radius is now recorded. The listings page's own read already uses a LISTINGS_COLUMNS projection; the unbounded .select("*") is in the SHARED useItemsFull hook, which the other 10 surfaces use. That is what makes this story risky rather than large: each consumer reads a different subset, and a missing column is undefined at runtime rather than a type error, so it fails silently in one column of one view. Do it with the app running, consumer by consumer. The US-2168 guard test (src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts) has a case that asserts the items_full read is STILL unprojected/unpaged — flip that expectation as part of this story so the gap can't quietly persist.

userStories.title: The listings table fires six unbounded reads, then filters and paginates client-side
userStories.description: As a reseller opening my listings, I want the table to load a page of rows from the server, so opening the page doesn't download my whole catalog and every photo row I own.
acceptanceCriteria: The cover-photo query stops reading every item_photos row for the tenant — covers come from a server-side per-item lowest-sort_order projection (view, RPC, or a join on the page's item ids)
The four secondary `listings` reads are scoped to the item ids on the current page rather than the whole tenant
Search, tab filtering and sort execute server-side so the client never needs the full set to render a page
Tab counts keep coming from the existing grouped count (useInventoryStatusCounts), not from loaded rows
Row-count parity is asserted against the current client-side behaviour so the migration can't silently change what a tab shows
userStories.notes: [P1][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. listings.tsx issues items_full (all rows) + listings ×4 (:708, :749, :786, :853) + item_photos (:817). The item_photos read is the worst: no filter or limit, so it pulls EVERY photo row for the tenant to pick one cover per item — a 500-item seller with 8 photos each transfers ~4,000 rows to render 50 thumbnails. Depends on US-2167. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. DONE: all five per-row detail reads (platform chips, draft metadata, publish issues, cover thumbnails, impressions/CTR) now scope to the rendered page via .in("inventory_item_id", chunk) keyed on pageRowIds, chunked through fetchInChunks (at pageSize 200 a bare .in() puts ~7.4KB of UUIDs in the query string and risks a URL-length rejection at the proxy). The cover read was the worst case — no filter, no limit on item_photos, so a 500-item seller with 8 photos each transferred ~4,000 rows to draw 50 thumbnails; it is now bounded by page size. The five queries had to MOVE below pageRowIds in the component: hook order is now load-bearing, and a 17-case source guard (src/test/listings-page-scoped-reads.test.ts) asserts the scope, the key, the chunking and the ordering. Safe to page-scope because all five are consumed only inside the row render — none feeds filtering, sorting, or the tab counts (those come from the server-side grouped count). NOT DONE: AC1's server-side lowest-sort_order projection (the client still picks the cover from the page's ordered photos — correct, and chunking preserves it because chunks are BY ITEM ID so an item's photos never span a chunk), and AC3 — search, tab filtering and sort are still CLIENT-side over the full set, because they depend on the still-tenant-wide items_full read (US-2167) and on scoreListability, which has no SQL equivalent. Those two ACs are blocked on US-2167, not skipped. KNOWN TRADE-OFF: paging now fetches per page, so a first visit to a page shows chips/thumbnails filling in; revisits are cached. That is the normal cost of not downloading the whole account.

userStories.title: No max_rows contract on any FlipDesk read — an over-cap seller could be shown a silently truncated catalog
userStories.description: As a reseller past whatever row cap PostgREST enforces, I want to be told my view is truncated, so I never make pricing or sourcing decisions on a quietly incomplete inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: The self-hosted PostgREST db-max-rows value in prod is established and recorded in vault/10-ops
Reads that could exceed it either paginate explicitly or request one row past their cap and surface a 'showing N of more' state
No FlipDesk surface can silently render a truncated set as if it were complete
The chosen cap is asserted in config so a future infra change can't move it unnoticed
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Perf] 2026-07-25 deep dive. Nothing in supabase/config.toml or docker-compose.coolify.yml sets a row cap, so the effective value is whatever the self-hosted PostgREST default is — unverified either way. If a cap IS in force, the unbounded reads in US-2167/US-2168 truncate with no error and no indication. Verify before assuming this is benign; the fix is cheap either way.

userStories.title: Listing Quality Score is built and tested but surfaced on exactly one page
userStories.description: As a reseller, I want each listing's quality score wherever I manage listings, so the one number that aggregates every ranking lever actually guides what I fix next.
acceptanceCriteria: The quality score appears as a sortable column on the main listings/inventory table
The score appears on the item page with its factor breakdown, so the seller can see WHICH lever is weak
The Active tab can sort or filter by score to surface the weakest live listings
Scores are fetched for the visible page only — this must not reintroduce an unbounded read (see US-2168)
The existing QualityScoreChip component is reused; no second scoring implementation is added
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. lib/listing-quality-score.ts is real and covered by listing-quality-score_test.ts, and src/components/flipdesk/quality-score-chip.tsx exists — but the only consumer is src/pages/flipdesk/autolister-drafts.tsx:783. This is the US-1897 'one 0-100 number per listing' and it is hidden in one corner. Highest visible-value-per-hour item on the 2026-07-25 list. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25. DONE: a Quality column on the listings table's Drafts and Active tabs, reading the persisted listings.quality_score (00476) page-scoped and chunked, keyed by LISTING id — items_full lateral-joins one listing per item and exposes it as listing_id, and every other listing-derived cell in the row comes from that same row, so scoring a different listing would put two listings' facts on one line. Error-to-empty-map fallback copied from the drafts cockpit (a missing column is 42703 and would otherwise blank the table). DONE: a ListingQualityCard on the item page showing the full breakdown + ranked fixes. That needed a second discovery — the edge has returned `qualityScore` on /listings/validate since US-1897 (flipdesk-ebay.ts scoreAndPersist), but ValidatePublishResponse never declared the field, so every client caller silently dropped it; now typed, with a useListingQuality(itemId) hook mirroring useRecommendedCoverage. Only score + blocked are persisted, so validate is the ONLY source of the breakdown. DONE: shared QualityScoreChip/QualityScoreBreakdown reused, no second scoring implementation (guard-tested). NOT DONE — AC1's 'sortable' and AC3 entirely: columnSort is typed `keyof ItemFullRow` and quality is not on that view, and the score is now only fetched for the CURRENT PAGE, so there is nothing to sort the full filtered set by. The clean fix is one migration adding l.quality_score + l.quality_blocked to the items_full view: sorting then costs nothing AND the extra per-page query disappears. Deliberately NOT done in this session — no Docker, so the db lane could not run, and adding the column to LISTINGS_COLUMNS before the migration applies would 42703 and take the WHOLE listings page down (the held-migration hazard CLAUDE.md calls out). Do it as its own commit with the migrations skill loaded and deploy order controlled. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-07-29: the HELD-migration claim above is STALE and should not be acted on. Every migration this story names is on origin/main and applied to prod (schema at 00503); PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is empty and the branch is not frozen. | Done 2026-07-30. AC1: quality_score exposed on items_full (migration 00506 — CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW appending the column, body verbatim from 00438, no DROP so dependents like the analytics RPCs are unaffected) and added to ItemFullRow; the Quality header is now a SortHeader(field='quality_score'), so the existing columnSort mechanism (listings.tsx:845) sorts the full filtered set numerically. AC2: the item page src/pages/flipdesk/item.tsx already renders QualityScoreBreakdown (US-1897), naming which lever is weak. AC3: columnSort applies on the Active tab, so clicking Quality surfaces the weakest live listings (and drafts). AC4: NO new read — quality_score rides the existing items_full row read; the page-scoped qualityByListing query (chip blocked-state) is unchanged, so no unbounded read is reintroduced. AC5: QualityScoreChip reused, no second scoring impl. Verified: npm run verify:db GREEN (whole tree re-applied from zero incl 00506), schema-version_test 18/18, 64 web tests (item-filter/flipdesk-lifecycle/quality-score-chip/listings-page-scoped-reads) green, tsc -b + eslint clean. US-1108 triple: idempotent view, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00505->00506 same commit, self-record footer, manifest regenerated. HELD migration — apply 00504,00505,00506 in order before push. VERIFIED.

userStories.title: Repricing applies one suggestion per click and never shows the rules that generate them
userStories.description: As a reseller with dozens of repricing nudges, I want to review, filter and apply them in bulk and see the rules behind them, so acting on my whole queue isn't dozens of individual clicks.
acceptanceCriteria: Multi-select + Apply selected + Apply all on the repricing queue
Filter by reason code (UNDERPRICED / OVERPRICED / STALE) and sort by suggested delta
The queue paginates rather than rendering every suggestion at once
The existing rules endpoints (/rules, /rules/actions, /rules/run) get a front end on this page instead of being server-only
A bulk apply is reversible via the US-2172 undo mechanism
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Pricing] 2026-07-25 deep dive. src/pages/flipdesk/repricing.tsx applies one suggestion per click (:113) with no select-all, no filter, no sort, no pagination and no undo. Rules already exist server-side at flipdesk-pricing.ts:1105-1201 with zero frontend. Note US-2161 folds this page into a consolidated Pricing route and US-2159 reconciles the two price-suggestion engines — sequence accordingly. | Partial 2026-07-30. AC1/AC2/AC3 shipped in src/pages/flipdesk/repricing.tsx: per-row + select-all-filtered checkboxes with Apply selected / Apply all (bulk via useBulkRepriceApply — cents-safe {listing_id, price_cents}, one request, confirm dialog + applied/skipped/failed result toast); filter by reason code (UNDERPRICED/OVERPRICED/STALE) and sort by absolute suggested delta (biggest/smallest change first); client-side pagination (PAGE_SIZE 20) with prev/next and a filtered-empty state. Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean; browser render NOT verified (repo has no @testing-library, convention is renderToStaticMarkup). REMAINING: AC4 a front end for the /rules, /rules/actions, /rules/run endpoints (server-only today; a separate rules-management surface, not built) and AC5 bulk-apply reversibility via the US-2172 undo mechanism (useBulkListingPrice/undoableFrom in use-listing-lifecycle.ts) — NOT wired because this page uses the cents-based reprice-apply path and reconciling it with the US-2172 dollar bulk-price undo path needs care plus a browser to confirm prices round-trip. | 2026-07-30 (AC5 done): bulk apply is reversible. applyRows captures each row's prior price (current_price_cents); the success toast carries an Undo action that re-applies those priors via the same cents-based useBulkRepriceApply, restoring exactly what changed and excluding rows the server skipped. This is a re-apply-based reversal (pushes the old price back), NOT the US-2172 undoableFrom/previous_price path — chosen so units stay in cents and match the apply mechanism; a reviewer who wants the literal US-2172 path can swap in useBulkListingPrice. Leaves only AC4 (a front end for the server-only /rules, /rules/actions, /rules/run endpoints). Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean; browser not verified. | 2026-07-30 (AC4 partial: read + run): use-repricing.ts gains useRepriceRules (GET /api/flipdesk/pricing/rules) + useRunRepriceRules (POST /rules/run); repricing.tsx renders a RepriceRulesCard that lists each rule with a one-line markdown summary (drop_pct / interval_days / brand / min_age / floor), a Paused badge, last-run date, and a 'Run rules now' button — surfacing the previously server-only rules and letting the seller trigger due drops. REMAINING on AC4: create/edit/delete/enable-toggle CRUD (the POST /rules, PUT /rules/:id, DELETE /rules/:id endpoints exist; a create form + per-row actions would complete it). With AC1-3 + AC5 done, this create/edit UI is the only piece left before US-2171 fully closes. Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean; browser not verified. | Done 2026-07-30. All 5 ACs complete in src/pages/flipdesk/repricing.tsx + src/hooks/use-repricing.ts. AC1: per-row + select-all-filtered checkboxes, Apply selected / Apply all via useBulkRepriceApply (cents-safe {listing_id, price_cents}, one request, confirm + applied/skipped/failed toast). AC2: filter by reason code (UNDERPRICED/OVERPRICED/STALE) + sort by absolute suggested delta. AC3: client pagination (PAGE_SIZE 20, prev/next) + filtered-empty state. AC4: a full front end for the previously server-only rule endpoints — useRepriceRules (GET /rules) list with a one-line markdown summary + enable Switch (full-rule PUT via ruleToInput so no field is wiped) + delete (confirm), CreateRuleDialog (POST /rules: name/drop%/interval/min-age/floor/brand), useRunRepriceRules (POST /rules/run) button, and RepriceActionsFeed (GET /rules/actions) recent-changes list; run invalidates suggestions+rules+actions. AC5: bulk apply is reversible — the success toast's Undo re-applies each row's captured prior price cents-for-cents, excluding server-skipped rows, via the same hook. Verified: tsc -b + eslint clean across all touched files. Browser render NOT verified (no component harness) — recommend a click-through of bulk apply, rule create/toggle/delete, and run-now. VERIFIED.

userStories.title: No undo on any bulk listing action — a 200-listing markdown is irreversible
userStories.description: As a reseller who just bulk-dropped prices on the wrong selection, I want to undo the batch, so one mis-click doesn't mean repricing 200 listings by hand.
acceptanceCriteria: A bulk action records the prior value per affected listing and returns an undo handle
Undo is offered in the success toast for a bounded window and re-pushes the restored values upstream through the adapters — not just locally
Undo reports per-row outcomes: a listing that sold or was ended between the action and the undo is skipped and named
Actions that genuinely cannot be undone (a published listing, a withdrawn offer) say so instead of offering a button that silently no-ops
Covers the bulk paths that exist today: price drop, bulk edit, bulk publish, archive, delete
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Listings] 2026-07-25 deep dive. CORRECTION (2026-07-25): the original note here said nothing in the codebase implements undo. That was wrong — it came from grepping only for bulkUndo/undo_token/bulk_undo. src/pages/flipdesk/autolister.tsx has a working undo for photo-GROUPING edits (undoLastGroupEdit / undoAutoGroup) using sonner's toast action, and that is the house pattern to follow. What genuinely had no undo is every bulk action on the LISTINGS TABLE: price, edit, publish, archive, delete. US-1348 specified 'multi-select batch + undo'; the batch half shipped and the undo half did not. Depends on US-2163/US-2166 landing the server-side batch path, which is where the prior values can be captured atomically. PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25 — the PRICE path only. /bulk-price gained a third body shape, `items: [{listing_id, price}]`, because undo needs each row to go back to its OWN former price and no shared price or percentage can express that; the response already returned previous_price per row, so the machinery was half-built by US-2163. The bulk-drop toast now carries an Undo action (15s, matching the autolister pattern). undoableFrom() decides what is reversible and is unit-tested: a row the marketplace REFUSED is excluded (it never changed, so restoring it would push a price nobody asked for), as are rows with no known/positive previous price and no-op rows. Undo is itself a real marketplace push, so it reports its own per-row failures rather than implying a clean revert. NOT DONE: bulk edit, bulk publish, archive and delete (AC5's full list). Publish and delete are arguably NOT undoable at all and per AC4 should say so rather than offer a button — that judgement is still open. Bulk END is the next most valuable: relisting is a real operation, not a field restore, so it needs its own design rather than a mirror of this one.

userStories.title: cross-push has zero tenant-isolation test cases — the seven-platform fan-out route is unguarded by tests
userStories.description: As the operator of a multi-tenant service, I want the route that writes sibling listing rows across every marketplace covered by the isolation suite, so a regression in its ownership checks is caught by CI.
acceptanceCriteria: tenant-isolation_test.ts covers POST /api/flipdesk/listings/cross-push: user B cannot cross-push user A's listing_id
The multi-platform fan-out shape and the own-platform shape are covered separately — they take different branches (sibling insert vs. publish the source row directly)
Each case asserts the RESPONSE BODY carries no draft_id and no per-platform results map, not just a denied status
The new cases gate only on TEST_USER_A_LISTING_ID, which is already seeded and in REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS, so they cannot land in the silently-skipped group US-2039 documents

Note for the record: steering the sibling lookup via draft_id and reading another tenant's platform_fields are NOT separately reachable over HTTP — both sit behind the same ownership check, so they are covered structurally rather than by their own case
userStories.notes: [P1][Security/TenantIsolation] 2026-07-25 deep dive. `grep -c cross-push services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts` returns 0. extension-writeback, delist-confirm, pending-delists and DELETE /item/:id are all covered; cross-push — the fan-out that inserts and updates listings rows for seven platforms — is not. The route's own ownership checks read correct on inspection (flipdesk-listings.ts:183-198, plus the US-1638 .eq(user_id) scoping at :296 and :312); this story is the missing CI guard, per the every-new-route rule in the tenant-isolation skill. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-25: two cases added to tenant-isolation_test.ts (multi-platform fan-out + own-platform branch), each asserting the response body carries no draft_id/results. Gated on TEST_USER_A_LISTING_ID (already seeded + REQUIRED). NOT yet verified locally — no Deno runtime in the session that wrote it, so the deno lane is CI-verified only. | Done 2026-07-29. Already present in services/edge-functions/src/tests/tenant-isolation_test.ts:294-359 — two cross-push cases: 'B cannot cross-push A's listing to other marketplaces' (multi-platform sibling-insert branch, platforms shopify+poshmark) and 'B cannot cross-push A's listing to the draft's own platform' (direct-publish branch, platforms ebay). Both call assertDenied AND assert the body carries no draft_id and no per-platform results map (AC3). Gated on TEST_USER_A_LISTING_ID, which is in REQUIRED_RESOURCE_IDS (line 89), so they cannot land in the silently-skipped group (AC4). AC5 (draft_id steering / cross-tenant platform_fields read are structurally behind the same ownership check) recorded in the case comments. Triage flagged this unwritten, but the cases exist and satisfy every AC. VERIFIED.

userStories.title: listings.is_active is a redundant second source of truth that defaults to true
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one authoritative answer to 'is this listing live', so guards and queries stop needing defensive comments explaining why they can't trust a column.
acceptanceCriteria: is_active is either a generated column derived from listing_status or kept in lockstep by a trigger — not independently writable
A never-published draft is no longer born is_active = true
The defensive double-filter in the storefront query and the eight-line 'don't trust is_active' comment in the delete guard are simplified to match
Migration follows the US-1108 triple: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the SAME commit, self-record footer
A backfill corrects existing rows where is_active and listing_status disagree, and its row count is logged
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Schema] 2026-07-25 deep dive. 00002_inventory_financial.sql:58 declares `is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, so an ordinary never-published draft is is_active=true. flipdesk-listings.ts:666-694 carries an eight-line comment on why the delete guard cannot trust it, and content-public.ts:1438-1439 defensively filters on both columns. Load the `migrations` skill before starting — enum/column changes plus a backfill. | Done 2026-07-30. migration 00504_listings_is_active_lockstep.sql: trigger trg_listings_sync_is_active sets is_active := listing_status IN ('active','relisted') on BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE — chosen over a GENERATED column because many paths write is_active and a generated column would ERROR on them (the trigger overrides instead, backward-compatible). Rule confirmed from the read paths: flipdesk-listings.ts:766 and the .in(['active','relisted']) queries in flipdesk-ebay.ts / jobs-credentials-refresh.ts treat relisted as live, so a status='active'-only rule would have wrongly hidden relisted listings. AC2: a never-published draft (status='draft') is now is_active=false on insert. AC3: dropped the redundant .eq('is_active',true) from content-public.ts loadStorefrontListings (kept the authoritative listing_status='active'); rewrote the two 'don't trust is_active / defaults TRUE' comments in flipdesk-listings.ts (GUARD 1 + wasPublishedUpstream) to reflect the derived mirror and the published-draft nuance is_active still can't capture. AC4: US-1108 triple — idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00503->00504 in the same commit, self-record footer; migration-manifest.ts regenerated. AC5: DO-block backfill corrects rows where is_active is distinct from the derived value and RAISE NOTICEs the corrected count. Verified: schema-version_test.ts 18/18, deno check + deno lint clean on all touched files. HELD migration (PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md) — committed locally, NOT pushed; db-lane verify:db not run (Docker down on the authoring host). VERIFIED.

userStories.title: perf: paginate/project useItemsFull to bound FlipDesk reads
userStories.description: As a seller with a large inventory, I want list views to load a bounded page, so routes don't download+hold my whole catalog in memory.
acceptanceCriteria: hooks/use-items-full.ts stops doing unbounded select('*'); provides a projected lightweight list query (id + display columns) with pagination/range
Full rows fetched only for the detail canvas that needs them
Six+ consumers (pipeline, prep, overview, composer, item, reconciliation) updated to the bounded/projected query without behavior regressions
userStories.notes: Audit 2026-07-26 perf (HIGH). DEFERRED (needs runtime verification): useItemsFull returns the full denormalized ItemFullRow[] that all 6 consumers (pipeline/prep/overview/composer/item/reconciliation) group/filter/sort CLIENT-SIDE. Adding pagination requires reworking each consumer AND driving the app to confirm kanban grouping / prep queue / reconciliation matching still work. Cannot verify headlessly (no runtime/QA). Ship only after driving the FlipDesk flows. | Scoped 2026-07-30, NOT started — recording why the DEFERRED still stands so the next attempt does not re-derive it. ItemFullRow is 61 columns and the heavy ones are all genuinely consumed, so this is not a drop-unused-columns job: comps -> src/components/flipdesk/comp-editor.tsx + src/lib/comps.ts; measurements -> composer/measurements-card.tsx + measurement-photo-editor.tsx; ai_field_sources -> composer/measurements-card.tsx + src/pages/flipdesk/prep.tsx:285; item_description -> composer.tsx:587/614/1514 + listings.tsx:1263; sold_at_raw -> listings.tsx:482; payout_reference -> src/lib/csv-export.ts:65. Both CSV exporters (src/lib/items-csv.ts, src/lib/csv-export.ts) serialize the WHOLE row, so any projected list query needs a separate full-row path or the exports silently lose columns. The real blocker is the shared cache key: use-items-full.ts documents that all consumers MUST share one queryKey AND one queryFn (same key + divergent queryFn means whichever route mounts first wins, and the others inherit its ordering/freshness). Splitting into a projected list query plus a detail query therefore changes invalidation behavior across 6 routes — which is exactly the part that cannot be proven by tsc or vitest and needs the app driven. Adjacent US-2204 shipped the projection pass on submissions/inventory_items/grade_reports (commit aec9e6b6) and deliberately left items_full to this story. | PARTIAL 2026-07-30, commit 84a541a4 — the BOUNDING half of AC1 shipped; projection + AC2/AC3 still open. src/hooks/use-items-full.ts now pages with .range() (1000/page) instead of one unbounded request. This turned out to be a correctness bug, not only a perf one: PostgREST caps a response at db-max-rows and reports it ONLY in the Content-Range header, so supabase-js raises no error and a seller past the cap simply got a short array — every FlipDesk surface wrong in the same direction at once (kanban, prep queue, reconciliation matching) with nothing signalling it. bulk-pricing.tsx and grid.tsx already chunk with .range(); this was the one heavy read that did not. A full last page costs one extra empty request rather than a guess, because stopping early on a full page is the same silent truncation. Behaviour is deliberately IDENTICAL — same query key, same queryFn, same newest-first order, same fully materialized ItemFullRow[] — so the six client-side-grouping consumers are untouched and this needed no runtime QA, which is what made it shippable while the rest of the story is still DEFERRED. 9 tests in src/hooks/__tests__/use-items-full.test.ts (supabase mocked at the module boundary), negative-verified by relaxing the short-page check to <= so the loop stops after page one (3 reddened, reverted). tsc + eslint clean, build green, 226 files / 2845 tests pass. STILL OPEN and still blocked on driving the app: the column projection and the list-vs-detail split, because all six routes share one query key AND one queryFn by design (divergent queryFns hand every route whichever mounted first), and both CSV exporters (src/lib/items-csv.ts, src/lib/csv-export.ts) serialize the whole row so a projected list query needs a separate full-row path.

userStories.title: perf: column-projection pass on hot tables + parallelize publish-fail loop
userStories.description: As the platform, I want lean queries on hot paths, so we transfer and hold less data.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace select('*') with explicit column projection on hot reads (items_full/inventory_items, listings, submissions, grade_reports; csv export selects only exported columns)
flipdesk-autolister.ts:2489 markPublishJobFailed loop uses Promise.all/batched concurrency
Skip count-only select('*', {head:true}) false positives
userStories.notes: Audit 2026-07-26 perf (LOW). PARTIAL: parallelize of the publish-fail loop committed (flipdesk-autolister.ts). DEFERRED: the broad select(*)->explicit-projection pass on hot tables (items_full/inventory_items/listings/submissions/grade_reports) needs per-query verification — a dropped column is a silent correctness bug, not caught statically where row types are loose. Do per-query with runtime checks. | Partial 2026-07-30 (aec9e6b6). SHIPPED the projection pass on the submissions/inventory_items/grade_reports hot reads: src/pages/submissions.tsx (SUBMISSION_LIST_COLUMNS on both list queries + the unpaginated exportSubmissionsCsv), src/pages/dashboard.tsx (RECENT_SUBMISSION_COLUMNS), src/pages/inventory.tsx (INVENTORY_LIST_COLUMNS), src/pages/new-submission.tsx (LINKABLE_ITEM_COLUMNS on the link-to-item dropdown, previously every ungraded item in the workspace), src/components/dashboard/grade-charts.tsx (CHART_SUBMISSION_COLUMNS/CHART_REPORT_COLUMNS). Each read is typed as Pick<Row, ...> of its projection, so the 'silent dropped column' risk the DEFERRED note raised becomes a tsc error -- that is what made the pass safe without runtime probes. AC2 (markPublishJobFailed Promise.all in cancelPublishBatch, flipdesk-autolister.ts:2503) was already committed. AC3 satisfied: count-only select('*',{head:true}) left alone. New guard src/test/hot-read-projections.test.ts (12 cases) pins the six reads and treats head:true as an explicit pass. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, npm run lint clean, npm test 224 files/2821 tests pass, npm run build green. Audited and deliberately NOT projected: listings (already column-projected at every multi-row call site; only two single-row .maybeSingle/eq-id reads remain), the admin consoles and edge accuracy-tracking.ts (loose row types, so a dropped column would NOT be caught statically -- the exact hazard the DEFERRED note named), and the SKU-merge/GDPR-export paths which need the whole row. STILL OUTSTANDING: items_full -- src/hooks/use-items-full.ts:52 is still select('*') and unpaginated. That is owned by US-2188 (paginate/project useItemsFull); this story closes when US-2188 lands.

PARTIAL: RSS <dc:creator> now emitted from the post author byline (falls back to "GradeThread Team") — added the author byline column to the public posts LIST projection + PublicPostListItem (additive, deno+tsc clean). STILL DEFERRED: per-tag <category> (needs a blog_post_tags fetch on the shared cached list endpoint) and the cert/passport gallery image[] JSON-LD (blocked on stable non-signed image URLs + SSR/SPA parity).
