AiExtractResponse in src/hooks/use-ai-extract.ts declares ebay_pending, attributes and ebay_category_query, which the server already returns but the web type omits.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. Server already emitted ebay: null + ebay_pending: true; both clients now read the flag instead of the dead ebay branch. WEB: extracted planEbayPrepRefresh into src/lib/ai-ebay-prep.ts (pure) and replaced the never-firing 'if (result.ebay)' block in composer.tsx with it — refresh inventory_item_ebay immediately AND again after 25s, plus honest pending copy; inline-block precedence kept so an older/future edge that inlines the result still works. AiExtractResponse now declares ebay_pending, attributes and ebay_category_query. iOS: AIExtractResponse decodes ebay_pending (decodeIfPresent ?? false, so an older edge is NOT pending), the store carries ebayPendingCategory, AIFillReview gained ebayCategoryPending as an OPTIONAL Bool (a non-Optional defaulted property would break synthesized decode of disk-cached reviews — the AIExtractResponse.attributes trap), the review sheet renders a 'Finding the eBay category' section instead of omitting it, and the manager schedules a follow-up inventory pull 25s after completion so the background-persisted category appears without opening the specifics editor. userStories.title: Depop/Etsy/Shopify publish pushed item photos with neither exclusion every other publish path applies
userStories.description: As a seller cross-listing to Depop, Etsy or Shopify, I want my care-label and price-tag photos kept off the marketplace, so that a name on a care label or my cost basis is never published as listing imagery.
acceptanceCriteria: resolveImageUrls in services/edge-functions/src/lib/marketplace-adapters/{depop,etsy,shopify}.ts runs filterListablePhotos, so 'internal' (price tags, receipts) and 'measurement' (the MeasureCard frame) are never pushed, matching flipdesk-ebay.ts.

Those three adapters resolve each URL through publicItemPhotoUrl (services/edge-functions/src/lib/item-photo-storage.ts) instead of getPublicUrl on the hardcoded item-photos bucket, so a sensitive photo whose bytes are in the private bucket is skipped rather than pushed as a URL that 404s.

publicItemPhotoUrl is the ONE definition of 'may this photo go to a public marketplace': flipdesk-ebay.ts's ebayPublicPhotoUrl delegates to it, so eBay's existing behaviour is unchanged and the four platforms cannot drift again.

A deno test asserts publicItemPhotoUrl returns null for a tag/tag_2/certificate row with an empty photo_url, returns the stored photo_url when one is present, and returns a public item-photos URL for a non-sensitive row.

The US-2265 source guard in tests/item-photo-storage_test.ts covers these files, so a future adapter that hardcodes the public bucket fails CI unless it justifies the site with an inline item-photo-url-ok marker.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. Found by the US-2265 source guard, fixed in the same commit. Extracted publicItemPhotoUrl into lib/item-photo-storage.ts as the single 'may this photo go to a public marketplace' rule; flipdesk-ebay.ts's ebayPublicPhotoUrl now delegates to it (behaviour unchanged there). depop/etsy/shopify resolveImageUrls now select photo_type, run filterListablePhotos, and resolve through publicItemPhotoUrl — so 'internal' price-tag/receipt photos and the MeasureCard frame are no longer pushed, and a care-label/certificate photo in the private bucket is skipped instead of being sent as a 404 URL. Note the pre-existing eBay behaviour kept deliberately: a sensitive row with an ALREADY-POPULATED photo_url (web uploaded every type to the public bucket) is still publishable, because live listings point at those URLs; only the private-bucket case is refused.

userStories.title: Verified-seller credential block froze at publish, so older listings advertise a stale graded count
userStories.description: As a verified seller, I want the "N items independently graded" block on my live eBay listings to reflect my CURRENT grade count and average, so that a buyer comparing two of my listings does not see 13 items on one and 19 on the next.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/seller-credentials.ts exports findSellerCredentialBlock + refreshSellerCredentialBlock: pure, walks <div> depth from the marker so ONLY the block element is replaced and the trailing "Graded by GradeThread — Condition Grade X — Cert #GT-…" line (appended after it by applyGradeListingPromotion) survives byte-for-byte.

refreshSellerCredentialBlock returns null when the description carries no block, an unrecognised shape after the marker, or an unclosed element — a refresh NEVER injects the block into a description that did not already have one.

POST /api/jobs/credentials-refresh (routes/jobs-credentials-refresh.ts) sweeps verified + embed-opted-in sellers and revises the LIVE eBay description of their GRADED items only: platform=ebay, a real platform_offer_id, listing_status active/relisted, listing_origin != ebay, inventory_items.grade_value not null.

The swap is applied to the LIVE offer description read back via getOffer, not to the stored copy, so a revise changes the block and cannot clobber eBay-side drift; listings.listing_description and (when it carries a block) inventory_items.description are then brought in line.

Cost control: the stored copy is compared FIRST so a steady-state run makes ZERO eBay calls; eBay writes per run are capped (default 100, system_settings credentials_refresh.max_per_run) with credentials_refresh.enabled as a kill-switch; candidates are ordered least-recently-updated first so a backlog larger than the cap rotates; a capped run reports capped:true and logs it rather than reading as "all current".

Job-secret gated (requireJobSecret) + overlap-locked (acquireJobLock, 600s lease); registered in CRON_REGISTRY (daily 40 5 * * *) with COOLIFY.md / CRON_SETUP.md / launch-checklist.md regenerated and the deploy.md cron count bumped; tenant-isolation_test.ts proves a user JWT and a bogus secret both 401.

Deno tests cover the swap: stale->fresh count, cert line and disclosure block preserved, idempotent second pass, null for no-block/unrecognised/unclosed, nested divs, and a stats-less block gaining a stats line.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. eBay bans active content in descriptions (no script/iframe/remote include) and bans off-eBay links, so a published block can never self-update — a scheduled REVISE is the only compliant fix (eBay allows description revises any time, free, even on a listing with sales). Scoped to graded listings per the operator ask. No migration: the kill-switch/cap read through getSetting with code fallbacks, and the round-robin uses listings.updated_at (bumped by the write itself) instead of a new last-refreshed column. Pre-existing Windows-only test failures on this host (brand-style-coverage readdir path, sizing-chart-parity + authenticity-references CRLF diffs) verified to fail on a clean tree too.

userStories.title: iOS-captured tag/tag_2/certificate photos render blank on web: the private bucket has no web display path
userStories.description: As a seller who catalogs on iPhone and finishes the listing on my laptop, I want my Garment Tag photos to actually appear on the web, so that I can see and reorder the shots I took.
acceptanceCriteria: A web helper resolves a display URL for a PRIVATE-bucket item photo: when isSensitivePhotoType(photo_type) is true (src/lib/constants.ts SENSITIVE_PHOTO_TYPES = tag, tag_2, certificate) AND photo_url is empty, it mints a signed URL on the submission-images bucket with TTL <= 900s (reusing SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS from src/lib/storage.ts), never getPublicUrl - the existing src/lib/__tests__/signed-url-ttl.test.ts scan must keep passing.

itemPhotoThumb (src/lib/images.ts) no longer returns an empty string for these rows. Today: iOS writes photo_url as '' for private uploads and never writes thumbnail_url (ios/GradeThread/Upload/ItemPhotoInsert.swift has no thumbnail field), so itemPhotoThumb falls through both branches and yields '' - which renders as a broken img.
Every web surface that renders item photos resolves these: photo-manager.tsx, photo-uploader.tsx, ebay-view-item-preview.tsx, autolister.tsx, listings.tsx, and the composer photos card.

Signed URLs are cached per storage_path until shortly before expiry so a scrolling gallery does not re-sign every frame (mirror of iOS PhotoSignedURLProvider's refreshSkew), and a failed mint degrades to a labelled placeholder rather than a broken image icon.

A vitest asserts the resolver: signed (path contains /object/sign/) for tag/tag_2/certificate with empty photo_url; the stored photo_url untouched for a web-uploaded tag that HAS one; the public URL for front/back; and empty input yields no request.

A vitest asserts a private-bucket photo is never handed to a PUBLIC destination from the client (eBay preview, share, export) - the display URL is short-lived and must not be persisted onto a listing.
The DB is NOT the problem and no migration is needed: the item_photos row, storage_path and bytes are all correct today. This is purely a client read path.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. New async resolver src/lib/item-photo-url.ts (resolveItemPhotoDisplayUrl + needsSignedDisplayUrl + itemPhotoPublishUrl), hook src/hooks/use-item-photo-url.ts, and drop-in <ItemPhotoImg> (src/components/flipdesk/item-photo-img.tsx). Sensitive (tag/tag_2/certificate) rows with an empty photo_url are signed via storage.ts getImageUrl (submission-images, SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS now exported = 900s), cached per storage_path with a 60s refresh skew; a failed mint degrades to a labelled placeholder. itemPhotoThumb (src/lib/images.ts) is intentionally UNCHANGED because it is synchronous and cannot mint a signed URL; instead every named surface routes through ItemPhotoImg: photo-manager grid + full-size viewer, photo-uploader, ebay-view-item-preview hero + thumbs, listings cover (guard admits sensitive covers), composer photos card (delegates to PhotoManager/PhotoUploader). autolister StagedThumb left as-is: StagedPhoto (src/stores/autolister-upload-store.ts) has no photo_type and holds web-session public uploads, so the private-bucket case never occurs there and the resolver is a no-op. AC6 pinned by itemPhotoPublishUrl (returns persisted public photo_url, never a signed URL). Verified: 17 vitest cases in src/lib/__tests__/item-photo-url.test.ts (AC5 table + AC6 guard + cache + full-original), signed-url-ttl guard still green, tsc -b clean, eslint clean on touched files. NOT browser-verified. VERIFIED.

userStories.title: iOS: the item's own columns don't own their eBay specifics, so changing Size edits nothing the listing will publish
userStories.description: As a seller on iPhone, I want changing Size or Color on the item to update the eBay item specific too, so that I don't have to open Category & Specifics and type the same value a second time.
acceptanceCriteria: Changing a structured column (brand/size/color/material/style) on the iOS item editor updates that column's eBay aspect even when the aspect's provenance is ai_extracted or manual. Today InventoryAspectSync.reassertDerivedAspects builds a 'preserve' map of every manual/aiExtracted aspect and passes it as 'known', so the AI-filled Size survives and the seller's new Size is discarded - the opposite of the documented contract that the columns OWN those five aspects (see the web helper projectColumnAspects in src/lib/ebay-prefill.ts and its tests).

The save writes BOTH aspect stores, not just one: inventory_items.ebay_aspects (+ebay_aspect_sources) AND listings.item_specifics_override (+item_specifics_sources) for this item's listing row. Today the save-time path writes only the inventory_items pair; item_specifics_override is written ONLY by SpecificsEditorModel (the Category & Specifics editor), which is exactly why the seller has to go there for the change to stick - it is the copy publish/revise reads FIRST.

The projection runs even when the item has no eBay category selected yet. Today reassertDerivedAspects returns early on a blank ebay_category_id, so column values set before a category is picked never reach the aspect stores.

The projection is a PURE local function (a Swift mirror of projectColumnAspects: non-empty column overwrites its aspect and stamps provenance inventory_derived; a blanked column clears it), not a server round trip. Today every save calls EbayAspectsService.deriveAspects, so a save costs a network call and a transient failure silently no-ops via try?.

An XCTest asserts the three rules directly: an ai_extracted Size aspect IS overwritten by a changed Size column; a non-column aspect (e.g. Department, Pattern) is left untouched; and a cleared column clears its aspect.

A deno or vitest drift guard asserts the iOS column-to-aspect name mapping matches the web/edge registry (services/edge-functions/src/lib/aspect-registry.ts, vendored to src/lib/ebay-aspect-registry.json), so the two platforms cannot disagree on which aspect a column owns.

Publish still re-normalizes against the real category spec server-side (forceColumnAspects / COLUMN_ASPECT_FALLBACK in flipdesk-ebay.ts), so a raw column value outside eBay's allowed list is still corrected at publish - this story does not change that.

userStories.title: Composer: Save/publish sat at the bottom of a thirteen-card page, so every save meant scrolling the whole form
userStories.description: As a seller editing a listing on the web, I want Save and Submit to eBay reachable without scrolling, so that saving a small change costs one click instead of a full-page scroll.
acceptanceCriteria: The Save/publish action row renders inside the composer's sticky preview rail (the @4xl:sticky column), FIRST in that rail so it stays on screen while the seller works anywhere in the form; the Listing preview follows it, because the sticky container clips at the viewport bottom and the button must never be what gets cut.
Exactly one instance of the row exists: declared once as actionRow and rendered once. No small-screen duplicate, which would put two identically-labelled Save buttons in the accessibility tree.

The notices that explain a blocked save (missing required specifics, the spec-vs-description mismatch, the live-listing warning) render in the rail directly BELOW the row, so a disabled button and its reason are visible together; they sit below the row so the button does not move as notices appear and clear.

The publish CONFIG cards stay editable and stay in the editor column: PushToCard, ListingKit and ScheduleCard render after StorageSkuCard and before the rail. ScheduleCard stays out of price-card.tsx.

US-2252/US-2253's guarantee is preserved by the control rather than by card order: the publish button names its destination in its own label and is disabled with 'Pick at least one marketplace' when pushPlatforms is empty. Asserted against the button's own source.

src/lib/__tests__/composer-anchors.test.ts is updated, not deleted: it now anchors on the {actionRow} render site rather than a className (the old anchor broke on a class change and took three tests with it), and asserts rail composition, notice placement, config-card placement and the button-level gate.
npx impeccable detect on composer.tsx stays clean, and the row wraps rather than overflowing the narrower rail (the publish label can read 'Save & schedule for Jul 30, 2026, 3:00 PM CDT').
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. actionRow extracted to a const and rendered first in the sticky rail, with the blocker notices moved in under it; PushToCard/ListingKit/ScheduleCard relocated INTO the editor column (they were left stranded below the grid with no button under them once the CTA moved up). Reframed US-2252/US-2253's guarantee honestly rather than deleting it: 'config directly above the CTA' was a layout expression of 'the CTA cannot outrun the channel picker', and a sticky CTA has no 'below' — so the invariant is now asserted against the button itself (names its destination, disables with a reason when pushPlatforms is empty). composer-anchors.test.ts rewritten to anchor on the {actionRow} render site instead of a className; the old anchor was a className string and my class change alone took three tests down, which is the real lesson. 14 tests pass; full web suite back to its single pre-existing failure (heading-outline needs a built dist). tsc, eslint and impeccable clean.

userStories.title: iOS item screen keeps drawing a SwiftData row the sync deleted, so it renders blank with no error
userStories.description: As a seller on iPhone, I want the item screen to stay usable after a background sync, so that finishing a grade doesn't leave me staring at an empty screen I have to back out of and reopen.
acceptanceCriteria: ItemCanvasView detects that the object it holds is no longer the live store row and refuses to draw it: a @Query on the item id classifies 'removed' (no live row - the merge's prune deleted it) vs 'replaced' (a live row exists for the id but is a DIFFERENT instance, i.e. delete-and-reinsert). Reference identity is load-bearing: an id comparison calls the replaced case healthy.

In either state the screen shows an explicit recovery (ContentUnavailableView + 'Back to inventory') instead of a form whose every field reads empty - which is what the seller reported as the screen going blank.

The state is REPORTED: a Telemetry breadcrumb plus an item_canvas_stale_row event carrying item_id, reason and live-row count, fired at most once per appearance. This failure previously produced zero telemetry (nothing throws, nothing crashes - confirmed: iOS reports to the gradethread-frontend Sentry project and there is no error for it), so the trigger could not be identified from source alone. The event is what names it on the next occurrence.
An XCTest covers the classification rule for all three cases (healthy / removed / replaced) as a pure function, so it runs without a ModelContainer.

FOLLOW-UP, not closed by this story: WHY the row is deleted mid-session is still unknown. mergeItems prunes only when isFullItemSync (itemWatermark == nil), and grade completion posts .inventoryPullRequested; the paginated item fetch and SyncEngine.resetWatermarks are the two candidates to examine once the telemetry lands.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. Guard + telemetry only; the root cause is deliberately still open (see the follow-up AC). ItemCanvasView gained a @Query on its own item id and a staleRowReason computed from REFERENCE identity (live === item), because delete-and-reinsert leaves a live row with the same id — an id-based check would miss exactly the case that blanks the screen. Renders an honest ContentUnavailableView with a Back button instead of a form of empty fields, and fires a breadcrumb + item_canvas_stale_row event (item_id, reason, live_rows) once per appearance. Chose the guard over re-resolving the object into the view: threading a replacement row through a 2000-line view that holds the item as a let, with its own @State form snapshot, is a refactor I cannot compile or test on this host. Diagnosis evidence: iOS DOES report to Sentry (8 cocoa events in gradethread-frontend, newest 2026-07-24, release com.gradethread.app@1.0.4+318) and there is NO event for this — so it is not a crash and not a throw, which is what pointed at an empty-rendering view rather than an error. 1 new XCTest, unrun locally (no Swift toolchain); five ios/Scripts checks pass.

userStories.title: The AI description never lands on iOS: a composed paragraph is judged by a confidence bar meant for observations
userStories.description: As a seller on iPhone, I want the AI description to actually be filled in after an add, so that I am not left with a blank description to write myself.
acceptanceCriteria: AIExtractStore.composedProseFields exempts 'description' from autoApplyConfidenceThreshold: it is written whenever the column is unset, regardless of the reported confidence. The set is narrow and asserted to contain exactly that one field.

The never-overwrite rule still applies to it: a description the seller already wrote is NOT replaced, whatever confidence the AI reports. Asserted by a test at 0.99 confidence against a non-empty snapshot.
An OBSERVED field at the same confidence still stays an opt-in row, so this is not a blanket lowering of the bar. Asserted with brand and description both at 0.6: description applies, brand does not.
condition_notes stays subject to the bar - the prompt defines it as 'condition hints explicitly mentioned or visible', which is an observation, not composed prose.

RATIONALE recorded in code: the whole chain was verified working first (the extract tool schema declares description, the prompt instructs 'always return a description when there is enough signal', decodeExtraction keeps it, iOS FieldUpdate.assign has a case for it, and the iOS item sync both selects description and maps it to itemDescription via resolveUserOwned). The confidence bar was the only thing stopping it, and US-2267 raising that bar from 0.5 to 0.8 would have turned an intermittent miss into the norm.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29. Verified the whole description chain BEFORE changing anything: the extract tool schema declares description, the prompt says always return one, decodeExtraction keeps it, iOS assign has a case, and the iOS sync selects description and maps it to itemDescription. Everything worked except the gate. Fix is a narrow exemption (composedProseFields = ["description"]) from the confidence bar, because the bar judges OBSERVATIONS - a brand guessed off a blurry tag is a claim that can be wrong - while the description is composed FROM the already-extracted fields, so its confidence measures the model rating its own prose and is not comparable. Never-overwrite still applies, which is the rule that actually protects the seller here. This also corrects a defect I introduced in US-2267: raising the write bar to 0.8 would have made a missing description the norm rather than an intermittent miss, so that story shipped a regression for prose fields that this closes. 3 new XCTests, unrun locally (no Swift toolchain); four ios/Scripts checks pass.

userStories.title: Photo edit is silently unavailable rather than explained, so a photo that cannot be edited reads as broken
userStories.description: As a seller, I want to know why I cannot edit a particular photo, so that I stop thinking those photos uploaded wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: PhotoManager renders the edit (pencil) control for EVERY photo and disables it with the reason in title + aria-label, instead of omitting it. Omitting it is what produced the report 'those two photos will not allow me to edit them like the others'.

Two blocked cases are named distinctly: a sensitive type (tag / tag_2 / certificate) explains that the original is stored privately because it can show names and addresses and an edited copy would have to be saved publicly; a row with a null storage_path explains that the file is still uploading or missing.
The underlying refusal is unchanged - persistPhotoBlob still throws for a sensitive type, so this is presentation only and cannot republish PII.
npx impeccable detect on photo-manager.tsx stays clean and the disabled state uses opacity + not-allowed cursor rather than a colour-only signal.

OPEN, needs one fact from the seller: whether the two photos in their example item are typed tag / tag_2. If they are, the confusion is compounded by US-2273 (those photos also render blank on web because there is no signed-URL read path) and fixing that removes most of it. If they are not, the null-storage_path branch is the live cause and the upload path needs its own story.
userStories.notes: Done 2026-07-29 (presentation half only; the diagnosis half is recorded as an OPEN AC). Edit control is now always rendered and disabled-with-reason. Established while investigating: REQUIRED_PHOTO_TYPES is only front+back, so the web bulk-add path assigns detail (editable) and cannot produce tag/tag_2 - meaning photos added after generation only become non-editable if the seller uploaded them into the Tag slots explicitly, or if storage_path is null. Could not confirm which applies to the reported item without prod DB access, so both branches are named in the UI and the question is recorded rather than guessed. Full web suite: the three source-scanning tests that failed in a full run (dialog-dynamic-viewport, status-enum-parity, composer-locks) all PASS in isolation - concurrent-agent tree churn during the 5-8s directory walks, not this change.

userStories.title: Lock down SECURITY DEFINER functions: revoke EXECUTE from PUBLIC across public schema
userStories.description: Postgres grants EXECUTE on every new function to PUBLIC by default. No migration in supabase/migrations/ ever revokes it, and no `REVOKE ... ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC` exists anywhere. Because these functions are SECURITY DEFINER they run as the owner and bypass RLS, so any holder of the anon key can call them directly through PostgREST. grant_grade_credits and debit_grade_credits carry no GRANT/REVOKE statements at all; the revenue-dashboard functions (00215_revenue_dashboard.sql:273-274) grant to authenticated and service_role but never revoke the implicit PUBLIC grant. Impact: mint yourself unlimited grade credits, drain another user's credit balance, and read the full revenue and customer roster anonymously.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration revokes EXECUTE on all existing public-schema functions from PUBLIC, then re-grants explicitly to the roles each function actually needs.
`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC` so future functions are closed by default.
Every SECURITY DEFINER function is inventoried with its intended caller role; credit-mutating functions (grant_grade_credits, debit_grade_credits, refund/reserve variants) are service_role only.
A test or CI check fails if a new SECURITY DEFINER function ships without an explicit grant block.
Migration triple honoured: idempotent SQL, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped in the same commit, self-record footer.
Run `SELECT proname, proacl FROM pg_proc WHERE pronamespace='public'::regnamespace AND prosecdef;` against prod before and after and record both in the story.
userStories.notes: [P0][Security/DB] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] VERIFIED directly against the code in this session. Pairs with the guard_users_protected_columns gap — either one alone gives free grading. Fix both together.

userStories.title: guard_users_protected_columns leaves entitlement columns writable by the account owner
userStories.description: The users self-update guard (latest definition supabase/migrations/00402_buyer_subscription.sql:41-88) freezes 24 columns covering role, suspension, plan and billing. It omits included_grades_this_period, ai_actions_used_this_month, ai_actions_reset_at, past_due_since, billing_source and google_purchase_token. The RLS policy at 00076:22 permits any-column self-update and no migration revokes column privileges. A logged-in customer can run supabase.from('users').update({ included_grades_this_period: 100000, ai_actions_used_this_month: 0 }) on their own row and get unlimited free Claude Vision grading and unlimited AI actions, billed to Pearson Media.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirmed present on public.users: ai_actions_used_this_month (00024_ai_enrichment.sql:10), billing_source (00104_appstore_billing.sql:13), included_grades_this_period (00209_pricing_config.sql:107). Confirm ai_actions_reset_at, past_due_since, google_purchase_token before writing the migration.

userStories.title: release_job_lock has no holder check, so an over-running job destroys its successor's lock
userStories.description: 00094_job_locks.sql:63-70 defines release_job_lock(p_job) as an unconditional DELETE, and lib/job-lock.ts:71 always passes p_holder: null so a holder check is not even possible today. Scenario: autolister-reclaim has a 300s lease and a */5 schedule — lease equals interval exactly. A run taking 5m30s means tick 2 legitimately steals the expired lock at t=5:00, then run 1's finally block deletes tick 2's live lock at t=5:30, and tick 3 acquires freely and runs concurrently. Mutual exclusion does not degrade, it disappears, and the more loaded the box the more concurrent runs there are. Jobs where lease <= interval: autolister-reclaim, publish-batch-reclaim, grading-batch-reclaim, thumbnail-backfill, email-retry, ebay-pending-webhooks, newsletter-ab-finalize.
acceptanceCriteria: acquire generates a holder token, release passes it, and the DELETE adds `AND holder = p_holder`.
Every job whose lease is <= its schedule interval gets a lease longer than its worst-case runtime.
Test: a stale-lock steal followed by the original holder's release leaves the new holder's lock intact.

jobs-guarantee-pool.ts:26 and jobs-durability-aggregate.ts:23-36 acquire a lock and never release it (no finally). Both are daily so the lease expires first, but a manual 'Run Now' inside the lease window silently no-ops. Add the finally.

userStories.title: Weekly north-star email marks users celebrated before it sends, and loses the tail on any throw
userStories.description: routes/jobs-north-star.ts:150-260. The loop has no try/catch and the handler is try/finally with no catch (:65, :273). The north_star_weekly_log insert is at :173-180, the send at :210, and the next run's dedupe reads exactly that table (:90-100) — so a send throw permanently marks the user celebrated and they never get the email. Worse, selection is keyed to weekStartKey (:69) and the cron is weekly, so a throw at user 50 of 1000 means users 51-1000 get no log row and no email, and that week is never recomputed. Their digest and milestone emails are gone, not deferred. Same pattern for milestones at :230-250.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-user try/catch so one failure cannot abort the run.
The log row is written after a successful send, or written as 'attempted' and only marked sent on success.
A failed user is retried on a later run rather than being permanently skipped by the week key.
Test: a throw at user N still delivers users N+1..end.

userStories.title: One poison row can block the entire email outbox forever
userStories.description: lib/email-retry.ts:63-119 has no try/catch in the loop. attempts is only incremented after a send result (:83) and next_attempt_at only advanced at :110-117. A row where getSuppression (:66) or deliverEmail (:77) THROWS never advances either field, never reaches max_attempts and never dead-letters — and rows are ordered next_attempt_at ASC (:49), so it sorts first on every run and aborts the remaining 49 of the 50-row batch, every five minutes, indefinitely. The only symptom is a 500 from the cron. lib/condition-alerts.ts:254-290 has the same shape: last_matched_at is stamped after the work, so a consistently-throwing search is permanently the stalest and therefore permanently first.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-row try/catch that advances attempts and next_attempt_at on a throw, not only on a send result.
A row that exhausts max_attempts is dead-lettered and stops being selected.

Same fix applied to condition-alerts and to the payout sweeps (lib/affiliate-payout.ts:469-480, :495-497 and lib/consignor-payout.ts:549-556, which have no per-item try/catch and deterministic iteration order, so one poison item blocks every item after it on every run).
Test: a permanently-throwing row does not prevent the rest of the batch from processing.

userStories.title: eBay orders sync advances its cursor after swallowing a failure — permanent order loss
userStories.description: flipdesk-ebay.ts:3219-3226 wraps the entire orders pass in a catch that logs and continues, then execution falls through to an unconditional cursor stamp at :3490-3493 setting last_synced_at to now(). Scenario: a seller has 500 orders modified since the last sync, eBay 500s at order 200. Orders 1-199 are committed, 200-500 are never written, and the cursor now says 'now', so the next incremental pull asks eBay only for orders modified since now (ebay-client.ts:3398) and the 301 missing orders are never re-fetched. Sales rows, payouts, net_profit and the inventory_items.status='sold' flip are gone for good. The HTTP response was already 202 {ok:true} and the UI shows 'Synced just now'. The backstop cannot recover it: jobs-ebay-order-backstop.ts:85-100 selects stale owners by that same last_synced_at. Same loss without a throw when ORDERS_PAGE_CEILING is hit (ebay-client.ts:3503-3507) — it only pushes a warning string into errors[] and the cursor still advances. Shopify does this correctly: flipdesk-shopify.ts:357-363 gates the watermark on ingest.ok and lib/shopify-orders.ts:62-68 documents exactly this failure mode.
acceptanceCriteria: last_synced_at is gated on the orders pass completing cleanly, or advanced only to the max lastModifiedDate actually persisted. Mirror lib/shopify-orders.ts.
Hitting the page ceiling is treated as incomplete, not as success.
The sync response and the UI reflect a partial sync rather than reading 'Synced just now'.
flipdesk-ebay.ts:3149-3153 and :3128-3131 destructure away the Supabase error and increment salesNew/salesUpdated anyway — read the error before counting.
Regression test: an injected failure mid-pass leaves the cursor unmoved.

userStories.title: Concurrent token refresh disconnects sellers on providers that rotate refresh tokens
userStories.description: No advisory lock, mutex or single-flight guard exists in any token path (no pg_advisory, no FOR UPDATE, no in-flight promise map). The read-modify-write is check expiry, refresh, persist. Four connectors do this and all four persist a rotated refresh token when the provider sends one, which proves rotation is expected: etsy-client.ts:392-396, whatnot-client.ts:347-350, depop-client.ts, flipdesk-google.ts:353-355. Scenario (Etsy, 1-hour tokens): a user opens the Marketplaces page while the sync cron fires; both see expiresAt - now < 60s (etsy-client.ts:368) and POST the same refresh token; Etsy rotates and invalidates the old one on first use; the second call gets 400 invalid_grant; isPermanentEtsyAuthFailure classifies 400 as PERMANENT (:243) so the handler sets is_active:false and stores a reconnect message (:410-416). The user is force-disconnected by a race, not a revocation. eBay is not exposed (its refresh token is not rotated).
acceptanceCriteria: A per-connection advisory lock (keyed on connection id) around refresh, so concurrent callers wait rather than racing.
invalid_grant immediately after a successful sibling refresh is treated as transient (re-read the row and retry once) rather than permanent.

refreshExpiringEtsyConnections (etsy-client.ts:467) scans on a 24-hour horizon but delegates to getEtsyAccessToken which only refreshes inside a 60-second window, so the cron decrypts every active connection every run and proactively refreshes nothing. Fix or delete it.
Confirm whether Etsy/Depop/Google actually invalidate the old token on rotation — that sets the real severity.
Audit prod for connections deactivated with an invalid_grant refresh_error and offer affected sellers a reconnect.

userStories.title: Etsy and Depop syncs discard every per-record error and report success
userStories.description: flipdesk-etsy.ts:274-278 and flipdesk-depop.ts:269-273 (plus the adapter copies at marketplace-adapters/etsy.ts:371-381 and depop.ts:329-339) loop over receipts calling handleEtsyReceiptEvent, which never throws and instead collects failures into res.errors (etsy-orders.ts:192,225; depop-orders.ts:167,200). res.errors is read nowhere. Every failed receipt is invisible and the sync returns ok:true. Neither loop has a per-record try/catch, so a throw at receipt 200 aborts 201-500, and since every retry restarts at offset=0 it hits the same poison record forever — a permanently stuck sync. Mitigating: neither uses a real fetch cursor so the next run replays the window and self-heals, but Etsy's window is capped at 20 pages x 50 = 1000 receipts (etsy-api.ts:525) so anything aging out before the retry is lost.
acceptanceCriteria: res.errors is propagated into the sync result and surfaced to the seller.
Per-record try/catch so one bad receipt cannot block the tail.
A record that fails repeatedly is quarantined rather than retried forever at the head of the queue.

etsy-api.ts:68-76, depop-api.ts:69-78 and whatnot-api.ts:53-60 have no 429 handling at all — fetch then throw on !ok, with no Retry-After, no backoff and no 429-vs-4xx distinction. Route them through lib/retry.ts. Shopify (shopify-graphql.ts:98-220) is the model to copy.

userStories.title: Marketplace webhooks have no freshness window and one debug flag disables all four
userStories.description: Verification itself is correct everywhere — all four receivers read the raw body, verify before any DB write, fail closed when the secret is missing, and use constant-time comparison (or asymmetric verify for eBay). Three residual gaps. (A) isDebugAllowed('WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG') is checked at flipdesk-webhooks.ts:123, :201, :493, :1229 and skips the whole verify block when true; lib/env.ts:82-85 returns false in production and edgeEnv() defaults to 'production' when unset, so a bare container fails closed — but any staging or preview with EDGE_ENV non-production and the flag on accepts unsigned requests on the account-deletion path (mass seller disconnect) and logs headers plus 2KB of body verbatim. (B) No replay or freshness check anywhere. All four rely on event-id dedupe which is skipped when the provider's id header is absent (:756, :389, :512) and FAILS OPEN on a DB error (:770, :400, :595, :1290). eBay's notification.publishDate is declared in the type at :744-745 and never read; Shopify's X-Shopify-Triggered-At is never read. (C) fetchPublicKeyMaterial (ebay-notification-verify.ts:135-154) does getAppAccessToken plus a call to eBay's public_key/{kid} for any attacker-supplied kid, with no timeout and no negative cache (keyCache at :92 stores only successes), bounded only by the 600/60s limiter at main.ts:1025 — so an attacker can drive 600 unauthenticated outbound eBay calls per minute per replica and burn the app's API quota.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm EDGE_ENV and WEBHOOK_PAYOUT_DEBUG in staging, and whether staging shares marketplace_connections with prod. If it does, this is live.
A timestamp freshness window (+/- 5 min) on the eBay and Shopify receivers using the headers already sent.
Dedupe fails CLOSED on a DB error rather than open.
Negative cache plus a timeout on the eBay public-key fetch.

Depop's header names (x-depop-signature / x-depop-hmac-sha256 at :495-496, x-depop-webhook-id / x-depop-delivery-id at :512) are unconfirmed guesses. The signature failure mode is safe (401) but the dedupe failure mode is SILENT — if Depop uses neither header, every delivery is reprocessed with no error. userStories.title: Impersonation is unbounded, unmarked, non-revocable, and allows account deletion as the user
userStories.description: admin-impersonation.ts:43-132 gets the entry right: super_admin only (:44), users:role scope (:38), fresh step-up (:49), self and privileged targets refused (:54, :68-73), start audited (:116). Everything after the token is minted is open. No time limit — generateLink type magiclink (:90) yields a normal Supabase session for the target, access token plus long-lived refresh token, in the admin's browser, with no cap anywhere. No revocation on stop — src/lib/impersonation.ts:126-129 only redeems the resume token and never calls auth.admin.signOut(targetId), so a copied refresh token outlives the session. No marker — there is no impersonated_by claim and no server-side active-impersonation row, so every request made while impersonating is indistinguishable from the real user's. And destructive actions are fully available: POST /api/account/delete's only server-side control is the confirm string (account.ts:390); the password re-auth at :625-631 is client-side only. A super_admin can impersonate a disputing customer, cancel their subscription and delete their account, and every downstream record shows the customer did it.
acceptanceCriteria: A hard maximum impersonation duration, enforced server-side.
Stopping impersonation revokes the target's sessions.

The impersonated session carries a server-visible marker, and destructive routes (account delete, subscription cancel, marketplace disconnect, grading spend) refuse or require additional authorization while it is set.
The account-delete password re-auth moves server-side.

userStories.description: admin-audit.ts:126 restricts GET /export to super_admin and self-audits the export (:165). But the RPC it wraps, admin_audit_log_search (00227_audit_log_search_export.sql:69), is guarded only by is_admin() and is GRANTed to authenticated (00227:108-110), accepting p_limit up to 50,000 (:60). src/lib/admin-aggregates.ts:179 calls it with the browser anon client from src/pages/admin/audit-log.tsx:144, and the isSuperAdmin check at :116/:142/:182 is a react-query enabled flag, not a boundary. acceptanceCriteria: The RPC's EXECUTE grant is narrowed, or the function itself enforces super_admin.
p_limit has a sane ceiling.
Every call is recorded, whether it came through the edge route or the RPC.
Sweep the other admin RPCs for the same authenticated grant pattern.

userStories.title: High-impact admin routes have no step-up: feature flags, money, grade voiding, agent execution
userStories.description: Step-up coverage is inconsistent in a way that inverts the risk ordering. PUT /api/admin/flags (admin-flags.ts:68) toggles ANY feature flag with only the router-wide ops:write, while the far less impactful PUT /:key/rule (:210) requires both super_admin and step-up; a second unguarded write into the same table exists at admin-waitlist.ts:235. POST /claims/:id/resolve (admin-guarantee-pool.ts:89) draws the pool and grants reward credit with no step-up and no super_admin, the only money-moving route in the service without step-up. POST /:id/approve (admin-claims.ts:473) refunds the grading fee and grants a free re-grade with no step-up, and sits under grading:review, so revoking billing:write does not stop an admin paying claims. POST /regrade (admin-bulk.ts:380) supersedes up to 200 issued grade reports with no step-up while its siblings /credits:260 and /suspend:316 both have it. POST /retry with kind grading (admin-jobs.ts:387) voids grades under ops:write without ever holding grading:review. Prompt and exemplar DEACTIVATE (admin-grading.ts:530, :2083) have no step-up while activate does. PUT /baselines/:id (:3145) overwrites the expectation baseline the grader compares against. POST /agents/proposals/:id/approve (admin-agents.ts:267) executes agent-authored operational writes with no step-up and no super_admin.
acceptanceCriteria: Produce one table of every admin mutation route with its scope, step-up requirement and super_admin requirement, and get it reviewed as a policy rather than fixed route by route.
Apply step-up to every money-moving, grade-voiding, kill-switch and agent-executing route.
Deactivate is as dangerous as activate — gate it the same.
Cross-scope holes are closed: paying a claim needs billing:write, voiding a grade needs grading:review, regardless of which router the route lives in.

STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_SEC defaults to 24 hours (env.ts:76-79), so step-up is a once-a-day control, not a per-action one. Decide the real intent and set it accordingly — the file's own comment acknowledges this.
userStories.notes: [P1][Admin/Security] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. userStories.title: The admin scope drift-guard cannot catch an unguarded mutation, and one already shipped

Router mode correctly asserts the use('*') shape (:81-83), but admin-users.ts, admin-bulk.ts, admin-scopes.ts and admin-guarantee-pool.ts are all mutations mode, so a new unguarded .post() in any of them passes CI. acceptanceCriteria: The guard parses per-route rather than doing a whole-file substring match.
admin-bulk.ts:199 gets a scope.

userStories.title: src/lib/storage.ts uploadSubmissionImage is a working trap that bypasses the US-276 upload contract
userStories.description: src/lib/storage.ts:35 exports uploadSubmissionImage, a client-direct-to-storage upload that validates on client MIME only. acceptanceCriteria: Delete uploadSubmissionImage and deleteSubmissionImage.
